review_text:
I'm conflicted as to how to review Westwind as we had two different planes for our group of 16 family and friends (ages ranging from 25 - 60) who had completely different experiences on our flight over the Grand Canyon from Page Airport. My flight (which I'll refer to as plane 1), which was supposedly the NON-executive plane, had an awesome pilot named Mark, who communicated with us throughout the flight, pointing out where to look (and there's a lot you won't see/notice if you're not directed) and forewarning us of turbulence. His humor and constant, clear communication made a semi-scary extremely turbulent flight as comfortable as it could possibly be. A few of us threw up from the bumpiness, but we felt very safe in Mark's hands and were all happy with our experience.

Our other plane of 8 people however (plane 2), had an entirely different experience. This plane we were told was the "executive plane" - nicer seats, etc. However, unlike plane 1 which had secure shoulder straps and individual seats for each person, this plane only had waist belts, the last row of the plane was a bench, and their seats were not in a fixed position and so were aggressively sliding back and forth throughout the flight. This constant movement, paired with turbulence, resulted in everyone slamming their heads into the ceiling multiple times (confirmed by every passenger) and 5 of the 8 passengers vomiting throughout the flight (so much vomit that my mom (the guest of honor) had to clean out the plane after they landed while the pilot stood by watching).  One person got so sick they had to go to the hospital afterwards and 3 others were ill for the rest of the day and unable to participate in the activities we had planned. Of the 8 people on plane 2, only TWO people actually saw the Grand Canyon because the others were so sick, or scared that they couldn't look. 

To make matters worse, their captain, unlike ours, did not speak once throughout the entire flight. Not only did this mean they weren't getting told where to look (which you think would be a no-brainer for a tour like this), but it also made everyone incredibly nervous as they continued to hit worse and worse turbulence. Honestly, when I initially heard how terrible a time they had, I thought they were being dramatic, but when I heard THESE details (seats sliding around, heads slamming into the ceiling, and a captain who did not speak the entire 1.5 hour flight) and they were confirmed by every single passenger, I was furious. 

Upon landing, as the majority of our group was throwing up outside the airport, the captains told us that that was the worst conditions they've ever flown through and that they were cancelling the rest of the flights for that day. While I'm of course glad that I (and the lucky others on plane 1 were able to see the Grand Canyon, I'm also a little skeptical of Westwind's judgment to 1) fly us in such bad conditions and 2) fly half of our group on a plane that seems incredibly unsafe and with a pilot who apparently doesn't have basic communication skills.  That's not just "bad conditions," that is bad judgement and completely unacceptable and infuriating when lifes are on the line. And finally, it's really disappointing that a once in a lifetime experience was turned into a harrowing, sickening flight from hell.

My cousin told us that the very best use of our money in Alaska would be on a scenic flight around Mt. McKinley. Even though they are expensive, she told us they are worth every penny. So, I went inside to check out K2 Aviation. There were so many options: the McKinley Experience, the McKinley Flyer, or as long as you're spending that much money, do you go all out for the Denali Grand Tour? And then should we add a glacier landing? There wasn't much of a discount for kids; they actually recommend having parents take turns and go one at a time while the other parent stays with the kids and plays on the playground. I didn't like that idea at all, and it was raining. And then I realized we had missed the first flight on the schedule and would have to wait for the next one, a few hours later in the afternoon. And if it was raining in Talkeetna, would we even be able to see Mt. McKinley? We drove away and started to leave Talkeetna. But then my husband spotted the float planes and decided we needed to stop and check them out. 

He has a thing for float planes (from watching Northern Exposure); he's also attracted to buildings with vegetation growing on the roof. The sign says Mt. McKinley Scenic, but the business is called The Alaska Bush Float Plane Service. 

My husband was sold with the idea of landing on a lake. And Molly, the woman who sets up the flights couldn't have been more accommodating. The planes only hold five passengers, but Molly quickly offered to babysit our youngest while the rest of us went on a flight. Perfect! (She told us kids under the age of five usually fell asleep anyway.) She went and talked to the pilot and came back with a reasonable discounted family price. I couldn't decide whether to take the Explore Denali 1.0 Tour or the Explore Denali 1.2 Tour. (The 1.2 Tour is about fifteen minutes longer, takes you over the Climber's Base Camp area, and offers a view of the West Buttress Route that is used by most climbers.) So Molly told me we could decide in the air. Perfect again! 

We flew over the Talkeetna airport, over some rivers, up and over the clouds, and then we were in the mountains. I could not believe the view! The glacier lakes were incredible. It looked like someone had dropped blue food coloring onto the snow. We flew right by the south face of Mt. McKinley. But without our pilot, we really wouldn't have been able to identify which one it was. All of the mountains were magnificent. And we were so close! 

It was probably ten minutes into our flight before I realized I had a two-way radio on my headset. Our three kids didn't know they had radios until the end of the flight; we didn't tell them because I didn't want them all trying to talk to the pilot at once. I had them raise their hands when they wanted to talk, and then I passed them my microphone.

They pick you up super early and drive you to the little airport. We sat there waiting for about 90 minutes before we boarded the plane. That's a lot of wasted time. 

The flight was fine. They have twin engine Otters (those are the ones in the pictures) and single engine Cessnas. The Otters hold about 20 and the Cessnas hold about 10 so which plane you get on depends on how many passengers are flying. I suspect that some of the flight delays might be related to consolidating trips to fill the planes.

The flight itself was fine. It felt safe enough and fun if you haven't been on a small plane before. But you wear a headset and listen to an audio recording that sounds like it was made in the 1960s. Ours started late so it wasn't synced with what we were flying over. Then it glitched and started playing the safety briefing again. Then the pilot caught on and restarted the audio - from the start - so we were now way out of sync. Then he tried to zoom forward and it was a little better. But you get the idea - it's pretty canned.

The views of the grand canyon are good. You are much lower than any commercial flight so you see the ground much better but don't get a high level perspective. It's a big loop out and back trip. Most of the people on our flight were dozing off. 

Bottom line, it wasn't bad, but it wasn't something I would do again.

K2 arranged pick-up and drop off service for us at the Talkeetna Lodge.  The transfers were completed smoothly. Each customers has a window seat which provides excellent views and an opportunity for unobstructed photography.  Frequently the pilot would maneuver the plane so the passengers on the right side would have a view of a glacier/mountain/point of interest and then adjust the route so the passengers on the left side would have a similar view.

Due to the Swan Lake fire the visibility directly after take-off was less than ideal.   The pilot indicated this would clear up as we gained altitude and approached the mountain range.   He was 100% correct as visibility was excellent as we approached Denali.

review_text:

Both sides of the airplane get the views. The glacier landing was very cool, and we spent 20 minutes walking around the plane in the huge Sheldon Ampitheater. It is just an incredlble place! review_text:
I am not a big fan of flying. My fear of heights and motion sickness are the biggest factors. My wife and I were doing a Princess Cruise and she really wanted to see Denali up close and personal. We went out to the airport at Talkeetna and looked at the various different operations offering a flightseeing of Mt. Denali. K2 Aviation seemed to have the best aircraft and most professional facility. We opted for the air tour which included a landing on a glacier near the mountain itself. 

We were issued boots and then greeted by our pilot, Stan. Our aircraft was a vintage de Havilland Otter that had been upgraded with modern avionics and a turbine engine. It appeared to be a very well maintained aircraft. After a short safety briefing, we were  in the air, heading for the mountain. 

There really is no better way to see Denali up close. Weather plays a big factor in determining how close you can get to the mountain and what you can see, but we got lucky with our trip. The views were truly amazing and I managed to get numerous pictures as our pilot wound his way around the numerous mountain peaks. .  

Landing on the glacier was fun and the view of the mountain from that location was the best. One minute the peak was covered with clouds and then it was out in the clear.  

Soon we were all loaded up and heading off the glacier. After a little more canyon flightseeing, we were on our way back to the airport. 

We saw many interesting and wonderful sights on our 12 day Alaska cruise. Without a doubt, the K2 experience was the highlight of the entire trip.

review_text:
I am rewriting this review, as my first review was softly forced.  The pilot stopped the golf cart near the hangars and asked us to click the links and do the review on the spot…and then he checked our phones to see that the reviews were completed with a thank you screen showing.  While I understand they need reviews as a small business, soft forcing and checking doesn’t feel like it’s the right way to do it.  I’ve been on other plane tours around a couple of the other Hawaiian Islands, so I have reference points for comparison.

Pros:  We did a custom tour, which is supposed to be a combination of two tours, with circumnavigation of Maui and a tour of the surrounding islands.  The views of Molokai and the surrounding area were fantastic.  The pilot, Eric, was skillful and we felt safe.  He was a nice guy and tried his best to be a good guide.

Cons:  (1) I feel like the price of our combined tour was a bit high (around 1250 for two people) especially considering the total time was only about 1.7 hours, which is about the time of just one tour.  I feel like more time could have been spent around west Maui , Molokai/Lanai and Molokini rather than Hanna, which is comparatively not that impressive.  I would not recommend our tour to others, based on my experience and at this price point.  (2)  They could use newer planes.  The current single engine plane (Piper Archer) is very old.  The exterior looks old and the interior is in rough shape.  Again, it was safe, but the plane could at least use a new coat of paint, the seats need to be re-upholstered and the interior needs a good cleaning/vacuuming and wipe down.  Also, the control pod of my headphones was coming apart with interior wires showing, and all the headphones had earmuff covers that were dirty and almost coming off…they could use disposable ear muff covers and mouthpiece covers…these things are very cheaply available on Amazon.  Finally, the pilot’s clothes looked like they were not washed for weeks.  Again, I think the pilot is a nice guy and I have nothing against him, but both my wife and I noticed this and thought it was strange.  Cleanliness is very important…it’s the first things people notice and experience.  These are simple things to fix.  (3) They really need a shared office or at least a hangar where customers can sit down and wait and get checked in etc.  It seems all they have is a parking spot on the tarmac and a golf cart that they use to get customers directly from their cars.  This is ok, but this is just a tip based on what I’ve seen with other tour operators.  

I would recommend this company over a helicopter tour because it is better for a small group.  However, I would like to see some of the things I mentioned to change.  They have been in business for 7 years.  So I feel like some of these things should be addressed for their benefit and that of future customers.  All they have to do is go experience some other airplane tours on other islands (like Kauai for example) to get more tips on how to improve.

review_text:
We visited Ketchikan and did the seaplane excursion with Taquan Air Tours only about a month after a couple of highly publicized accidents involving the company in the summer of 2019. Even though the accidents occurred in close succession, it is important to understand how many of these excursions the company flies each day, each month, each year when no such accidents occur, and to consider how many automobile accidents happen daily on the interstate within just a few miles of ones home, or even at a nearby intersection, I think that the excursions do come with an element of danger, but not a ton more than driving to work each day. It seemed to me that our pilot knew his job very well, and that the plane was well-maintained, and that every precaution was taken to ensure a safe flight and landings. Having said that, this was, of course Ketchikan, Alaska, and the estuary/bay where we took off did have a small number of logs floating around that posed a potential danger during take off and landing, due to sometimes being visible only at the last moment. In fact, out of concern whether we may possibly have clipped one such log during take off, our pilot requested another pilot who took off shortly after us to fly by our right side to visually affirm that that the pontoon on that side had not taken any damage that might affect landing, which in fact it had not.
During the flight to Misty Fjords, the scenery was beautiful, and it was fun to land in one of the bays there and step out onto one of the pontoons for photos, which the pilot happily took for us.
In my opinion, all of the best adventures involve at least an element of danger, and the choice taken to avoid one perceived danger is all too often the choice that leads to a different totally unexpected accident, due to an overly-comfortable illusion of safety/security.  This excursion was one of our trips highlights. We enjoyed it a lot, and believe most visitors would, too.

review_text:
Last year, Taquan (pilot Dave and guide Mark Phillips) did an excellent job at getting us to Anan Creek.  However, due to our ship's limited time in port last year, along with poor tidal conditions, we were not able to actually get to the trail head and take our tour.  This year, we again booked our Anan Creek tour with Taquan and we were not disappointed.  From the bus drive to their terminal, to their check-in and flight briefing process, to the flight itself, and to the tour guide - Taquan offers a safe, informative and exciting tour.

The checkin and safety briefing process was thorough, yet efficient (quick).  We met with our pilot, Eric, immediately after the safety briefing, and he walked us down the pier to our plane.  Eric got us situated on the plane, and then our tour guide arrived.  To our pleasant surprise, our guide from last year - Mark Phillips - was again our guide this year!  Within a few minutes we were skimming across the water and taking off from Ketchikan.  Eric provided some commentary on various landmarks while we were en route to Anan Creek, and Eric's 45 minute flight from Ketchikan to Anan Creek was smooth and comfortable.  At one point as we got near Anan Creek, we encountered a rain squall, and Mark and Eric communicated and made some adjustments which ultimately allowed us to safely land at the Anan Creek landing site.

For any tourists taking a float plane to Anan Creek, it is important to be aware that at low tide there can be significant logistics regarding where/how you get to the Anan Creek trailhead.  When we arrived at Anan Creek, it was low tide - and Eric brought the plane to a small dock that was far enough off shore to avoid grounding the plane.  Taquan had arranged a small boat to transport us from the dock to the shore, and that worked out very well.

If you remember any tip from this review, it is this:  if you want to avoid the potential hassles and delays of low-tide arrivals at Anan Creek by float plane, make sure ahead of time that your pilot knows to putter into the entrance of the creek where the water is deep enough (even at low tide) for any float plane to drop off passengers just below the ranger briefing station.  It is not worth your time, or the risk of grounding, to make land anywhere near the docks or the hut.

Let me say here that our guide, Mark Phillips, was awesome.  Mark was friendly, knowledgeable, and he has the experience of having flown out to Anan Creek multiple times in the past.  Mark was able to provide direct in-flight guidance to our pilot when weather conditions got a bit hairy. The guide took us down a short trail and pointed out many signs of bear activity - scat (feces), claw markings on trees, and several plants that the bears had eaten. At the end of the trail (about 1/4 mile) was an open area with the fish hatchery.

Just as our group arrived at the fish hatchery, we heard muted "oos" and "ahhs" from another two groups that had arrived before us - bears! I reassured myself that Taquan Air had a better safety record than ProMech Air, until I came across the below article.

The article made me feel betrayed by Taquan Air, and stupid for not doing more of my own research. The Cruise Lines and the tour companies seem to be too driven by profits that they may not cancel flights when necessary due to bad weather and are enticed into telling customers lies about their safety records so people won't back out of excursions.  I still would've taken the flight had Taquan told me about the 2007 incident, but now I'll never fly with them again.

I'm giving a rating of 3 (wish it could be 2 1/2) because the Pilot, Kevin, was amazing and he seemed like an excellent pilot and made everyone feel very comfortable and deserves 5 stars, but the companies dishonestly about the crash in 2007 deserves ZERO stars.

Alaska News
As Southeast Alaska plane crash victims' life stories emerge, so do echoes of 2007 accident
Nathaniel Herz
June 27, 2015
He cited the 2007 crash that also happened during a tour of Misty Fjords, which an NTSB report a year later blamed on pilot error and inadequate supervision of the Southeast Alaska tour industry by the Federal Aviation Administration. Subsequent recommendations by the NTSB included the installation of webcams in the area and special weather training for tour pilots. 

2007 Misty Fjords crash

Weather in Ketchikan the day of the crash was unsettled, with scattered showers and wind gusts hitting 26 mph.

“Equally impressive are the flight challenges posed by such dramatic terrain and volatile weather conditions,” the filing said.

In the 2007 crash, Ketchikan’s Taquan Air Service had sent three planes on Misty Fjords flight tours.

All three planes were flying through a shallow mountain pass known as “the cut.” The first plane made it through and the third plane’s pilot turned around and took a different route after running into what he described as a “wall of weather” — rain, fog and low clouds — according to news reports.

The second plane, a de Havilland Beaver, crashed in a box canyon and slid 250 feet down an embankment. All five people aboard were killed.

The pilot, 56-year-old Joseph Campbell, had 25 years of commercial aviation experience, but only seven hours of flying experience in Alaska when he was hired by Taquan to fly that summer.

We were only in Talkeetna for one day and knew that Denali weather has a mind of its own. But to our delight the rain cleared and the day was perfectly clear, resulting in one of the most spectacular things we have ever seen or done!

We originally booked the glacier landing but the glacier was not in a safe condition for landing so we changed to the Summit tour. Last minute the Summit tour was cancelled due to high winds, so we sort-of reluctantly rebooked to the Denali Grand Tour since it would be the best option we could get. The Grand Tour was utterly spectacular. I was lucky enough to ride copilot, our pilot was fantastic and answered all of my nerdy airplane questions, and for 90 minutes we got to see the staggering views of Denali and the surrounding rivers, glaciers, and sister mountains up close and personal with INSANE visibility. We climbed to a total of 12.3kft and could see each peak in an incredibly personal and in-your-face manner as we weaved in-and-out through the peaks and valleys. 

90 minutes came and went so fast. Yes this can seem expensive to most, but damnit, do it! You will not regret it for a minute and you’ll have unreal photos to reflect on for the rest of your life. 

We are still in awe. Thank for the mesmerizing experience, K2! Just keep flying!

Booked this with my father who was up in Alaska visiting me. We originally booked the Grand Denali with glacier landing, and was told we'd be on a Turbine Otter-- which made sense, given they're the majority of K2 and every other Talkeetna tour operator's fleet, as they make excellent flight seeing planes due to their high wings and single engine. The booking was pricey, especially when an entire 185 could have been chartered for the same money (and we'd have had seats to spare), but being able to land on the glacier was worth it, we thought.

When we arrived we learned the glacier landing was scrubbed due to the warm weather. Not much to be done about that-- we were disappointed but in no way upset about K2 for it. And besides, the weather was as clear and sunny as I have ever seen Denali, and smoke from the local wildfires had shifted out of the area, setting up K2 with the opportunity to give an absolutely amazing trip.

Instead, they blew it. We were ushered not to an Otter but a Piper Navajo, whose twin engines and low wings make it utterly horrible for a flight seeing plane-- probably why neither Talkeetna Air Taxi nor Sheldon Air Service across the taxiway from K2 have anything like it in their fleet. It is, however, a bit cheaper to operate than an Otterof which there were about 4 on the ramp at K2 when we departed. The picture attached shows the view out my window. I spent the entire flight with them obstructing the views and making pictures more difficult.

I won't be bringing any other visitors back to K2. Taking a scenic around Denali is certainly an experience, but K2 absolutely blew it. I'll be taking future visitors elsewhere.

I need to reschedule the flight for 3 times because of Glacier Landing. When I asked a front desk person, when was the last glacier landing, she did not able to answer me which is quite awkward whereas K2 Aviation giving advertisement always with Glacier landing. So I need to choose only Denali Grand tour without Glacier landing which is fine cause they can not land on hard ice or weather contsraints. However, as a Company they should have keep the statistics or records when was the last glacier landing or the ideal time of Glacier landing chances so customer can plan accordingly.

The grand tour was good but it would be nicer if the pilot would narrate the navigation during fly as it was depicted on their website pages how would be the navigation and what mountains and peaks would be covered as well as an handly print out of this navigation so customer can enjoy the total journey fully instead of just seeing white glaciers from the top.

review_text:
I could not recommend taking a K2 flying tour more. It was the highlight of our trip to Alaska and one of the most unforgettable experiences I've ever had. 

K2 watched the weather carefully and made sure we went up at a time when the viewing would be good. We really appreciated their diligence about the weather to ensure a good viewing experience. Given the potentially flexible nature of the flight time, I would recommend planning only activities that can be rescheduled on the same day as your flight tour. We just did a local hike that day, so it was easy to flop our schedules to accommodate the flight time change. We also ended up on a better tour without paying extra since our rescheduled time was to go with others who had booked a longer tour.

The plane itself was comfortable and offered great views from every seat. He was also diligent about making sure everyone on both sides of the plane got to enjoy views of the best sights.

The one complaint I would have is that we were confused about being picked up for our flight. When we signed up, the form asked for a pick-up location and gave us a pickup time, but we were actually expected to get there ourselves. Getting there wasn't an issue, but the confusion about what we were supposed to do was frustrating. They also didn't call us when they knew our flight would be rescheduled. They were just going to wait for us to check in at the location to tell us. Luckily, our lodging owner called over there for some other customers and found out that they wouldn't be flying until the afternoon and let us know. We then called and we able to reschedule and clarify the pickup situation. This was frustrating at the time, but the experience was so wonderful, I am not docking them any rating points. The seating in the chopper is set by the computer based on the weight of all passengers in order to achieve a good balance, so there is no point worrying about where you will sit (you simply can’t control it). All the views were good though.

review_text: My Canyon Spirit  helicopter tour was part of a 2200 mile motor trip including Zion, Bryce, Monument Valley and Page.  The decision to view the Grand Canyon by air instead of hiking did not disappoint.  The weather for my 9 15 am flight was clear and calm and fellow passengers included a father/son from Germany and a senior couple from Wisconsin – all of whom were very excited for the flight.  The most amusing part of the trip was when our handsome pilot, John Paul, told us his favourite parts of the Grand Canyon after piloting the Canyon trips for a mere 5 days. As the audio briefly cut out all we heard was he had flown helicopters for 5 days !  Too funny!  (he formerly worked at the Las Vegas location)  The journey was smooth and gentle – like a flying couch – which is critical to those of us who suffer from motion sickness.  The temperature inside the helicopter was perfect – having been baked on stifling flights over Niagara Falls, Ontario, Canada and Canmore, Alberta, Canada,  I was pleased the pilot confirmed our comfort level several times.  The views are spectacular:  full of colour and texture.  Some passengers are interested in photography, others are content to soak up the views.  The richness of any experience is determined by what you bring to it – asking a few questions of the pilot who flies tourists over the Canyon every day brought a whole different perspective to the Grand Canyon experience.  For those of us not paying in US dollars its pricey but as a once in a lifetime flight it was worth it.  (And for ‘balance’ reasons I got to sit next to the pilot – it was tough but someone had to do it)

review_text:
My husband and I booked the Canyon Spirit, 45-50min tour with Maverick Helicopters as part of a 3 week tour around the west of America. We booked it online a month before we went through the chat option on their website, where they gave us a bit of a discount and all the information we needed.
We were told to book in advance because it gets so busy and booked up and we were really glad we did. We did a lot of research on the different options of people to fly with and it paid off because there's nothing we'd change about the one we did. It cost $544 for both of us, which is a lot of money but we'd totally recommend it.

We flew at 8am on Thursday September 15, 2018. It was a perfect time and day. The weather was amazing and it was all perfect for the flight. You have to get there about 30 mins before the flight and you're weighed so they can allocate you in the helicopter according to weight, to spread it out. You can't choose or request a specific seat. Fortunately my husband and I got to sit in the front and it was spectacular. The helicopter is largely glass and from the front you can see right down to take in the view. However, there is a great view from every seat and I really wouldn't worry about where you sit.

Each helicopter took 6 passengers, plus the pilot. 

Everyone has headphones and a microphone so you can all communicate with one another during the flight and ask questions. We were fascinated by the number of helicopters that took off at similar times but yet once you're in the air and going over the canyon you can't see any at all. It felt like you were the only one in the air and it's very difficult to take in the sheer scale of the canyon even when you can see a lot of it.

There wasn't anything scary about it or unnerving, we absolutely loved our first trip in a helicopter. 

We would thoroughly recommend this trip.

Straight up, this is the single most expensive activity we did on our whole honeymoon. We debated long and hard if we could justify the cost, and researched the other operators offering similar service. We decided to go with Maverick due to their air-time and route being the most appealing we found. With all the travel we want to do around the world it is likely this would be our only visit here so we dug deep and coughed up the money as we know we'd regret if we didn't do it. We were not disappointed! 

We knew there would be a few things that would have to go right for the best possible experience including the weather and our positions in the chopper. We came up trumps with both. We had a cracking day. No wind, so a smooth ride and excellent visibility. I can see people's frustration at being in the back row of the aircraft as you definitely get a better view up front and it is easier to take photos. (Though the bubble canopy makes photos without reflections tricky regardless of where you sit.) I had the good fortune of being the exact same weight as the pilot so I got a balancing seat opposite him with the little wifey sitting in the middle. The view from the back isn't terrible, but the front definitely gives the best experience. You just have to be lucky I suppose and I'm glad we were. 

The Canyon was everything we hoped for and a chopper flight is easily the best way to experience it in a short period of time. We headed to the lookouts afterwards and there is simply no comparison. The pilot was skilled and the commentary informative. Every twist and turn unveiled a jaw-dropping panorama of river, rock and plateau. You spend the whole flight with a huge grin on your face and wondering if it is all real. The 45-minute flight felt sufficient and immersive, I think the shorter one would leave you wanting more. Due to the cost, I don't think I'd do it again, but you'll kick yourself if you don't do it once when you have the opportunity! It is truly a once-in-a-lifetime experience I don't think you can replicate anywhere else in the world. I thought our heli-flight back home over the Great Barrier Reef was amazing, this takes it to another level.

review_text:
We decided on the Maverick Helicopter Tour as it seemed that they had newer equipment than the other tour companies in the area. You meet at the Tusayan Airport which is outside of the Grand Canyon National Park (It is just outside of Tusayan). They have a large parking lot and guest services building with a gift shop, vending machines and restrooms. Check-in is fast and easy. They do take your weight (no lying about your weight, as you actually stand on a scale) which they use to assign your seating on the helicopter to balance the weight. You can request a front seat but they cannot guarantee specific seating but will give you preference if you ask in advance. Once everyone is checked in the pilot will call out your name and give you a seat assignment. You are provided with a life preserver that you wear around your waist and are assisted in getting in the helicopter. Once in, you put on your headphones and get a quick safety check. (you should wear dark clothing without prints so that you don't get a reflection off the inside of the glass when you take photos). The flight is about 45 minutes and there are no restrooms on the helicopter and no stops until you get back to the airport (as my Mother always told me, go now or forever hold your pees). The seats are very comfortable (seating for 7 including the pilot) and the helicopter is surprisingly quiet from others I have flown in. The weather was clear and the flight very calm and smooth.

Once everyone is secure the pilot takes off and introduces himself and finds out a little bit about you. You initially fly over the pine forests and listen to a play list and commentary through your headphones. Then you fly out over the Canyon itself. The view is spectacular as the trees and land immediately end and fall away from view and you are now hovering 4,000 feet above the Canyon Floor! The pilot forewarned us just before we cleared the trees and got our first panoramic view of the Canyon but it is still breathtaking! The pilot describes the various areas of the Canyon and sights and flies along both the South and North Rims as well as along the Colorado River. You can ask questions through your headsets and the pilot is more than happy to respond and elaborate on his narration. Although we viewed the Canyon from the South Rim, the Rim Trails, the Bright Angel Trail and the West Rim, this is a unique "not to miss" way to see the Canyon if your budget allows.

After about 45 minutes we landed back at the airport and they took pictures of us by the helicopter (with or without the pilot) and using their camera and ours. Although not required or requested, we did give a small gratuity to the pilot which I'm sure he appreciated. When we got back into the gift shop they had photos on the wall that you could purchase as well as a dvd of your specific flight made during the actual flight. Unfortunately the camera on our helicopter malfunctioned on our flight so we couldn't purchase the dvd of our flight but because we had asked to buy the dvd they gave us a complimentary copy of their generic dvd of the helicopter flight (very considerate and professional). 

The price for the helicopter flight was about $300 per person for about 45 minutes but was well worth it. If you want to get a different perspective of the Grand Canyon, this is definitely not a tour to miss! I would highly recommend both the helicopter flight and Maverick Helicopters as the tour provider.

review_text:
Sorry - this is a long review, but there is some constructive feedback at the end which needs reading. 

Having booked with Maverick airlines last year to fly from Vegas to the South Rim on a small plane tour, one regret was not taking up the option of a helicopter flight. This year my wife, daughter and I had planned another road trip but coming at the Canyon from a different direction - on the train from Williams.

My first interaction with Maverick was by live chat on their website in February '15. Spoke to a lady called Elaine who was helpful and informative. My big question: the train arrives at 11:45am and leaves at 3.15pm - what would be the best option for a 40 minute Canyon Spirit tour? She suggested the 12:45 flight, with 12:15 check in. It would be 20 minutes in a cab from the train depot so plenty of time. No they don't have their own transport but cabs would be readily available and she gave me the number to call one in advance.

I wanted more time to think it through before booking and it was May before I felt confident to reserve 3 seats on Saturday the 11th July at 12:45. Maverick advised me that we were the only 3 on the flight and that they'd need at least 3 more before they'd fly. Same instruction as last year - call the day before to check in and confirm the flight.

Our holiday itinerary meant we'd be on the road a lot during office hours. I called Maverick from San Diego 2 days before to confirm and they told me they had still not sold any other seats but not to worry, they usually do. 12 hours later we were in Williams with the train the next morning. Called again - yes they had enough seats sold so the flight would go ahead.

At this point I started worrying about the taxi. I called the phone number to book one. Unobtainable. I googled cabs in the Grand Canyon, but only Flagstaff numbers came up. Just have to wing it then.

Arrived at Grand Canyon depot at 11:45 - no cabs. Asked a park ranger who gave me a number for Xanterra who arrange cabs, but no service on the mobile. 20 minutes passed and we were panicking. We ran into the El Tovar and asked the concierge for help - she called Xanterra who said it would be 45 minutes…+ 20 to the airport = flight missed. She called Maverick for us and I spoke to a guy…he left me on hold a while and came back to tell me a car would be there in 9 minutes. 

We arrived at the airport at 12:35, sweating! From that point we relaxed. We got weighed and bags stored. Our pilot for the day was BJ, who took us out to the helicopter for quick introductions. 

There were 6 people on the flight, organised by weight. The helicopter has 2 banks of seats, with 3 available in front and 4 in rear. My wife and daughter were in the front row and I was rear left.  Views were exceptional in the front seats and excellent for me in the back. Not so sure how people in the middle of rear would have found it. But it's luck of the draw. If you are light and slim, you will likely be in the front. 

BJ was an entertaining and informative host and kept us all interested and engaged throughout the flight. The first 5 minutes of the flight took us over trees and scrub, towards the lip of the canyon. Then jaws literally dropped as BJ took us over the edge. Imagine sitting on  a rollercoaster as it attempts its vertical drop…now imagine that drop is 6,000 feet down! What a feeling! There was significant clutching going on as fingernails gripped seats.

For the rest of the flight we navigated from south to north and back. The colours, the lines of evolution, the difference in vegetation - its not something you can easily see just walking around the rim, but up in the air the stunning vista opens up magically. 

On return we found that Maverick had organised for us to share a cab back to the South Rim so we could get our return train. In summary, Maverick provided us with a genuine highlight of our holiday, rescued us from potential disaster and stopped up when they needed to. for that, it was a 5* experience.

However, I have some constructive criticism to make re the booking process:

Shuttle transport should be available to get clients from the South Rim to the airport. If you book as a package with the train company, or with Maverick airlines as part of a tour you do. As an independent booking you don't. It would take away the stress completely to know that you would be picked up and dropped off at the right time. Both trips cost us $22 + tip. I'd be happy to see this included in the overall price, just for peace of mind.

The on-line live chat team should be aware of the cab limitations from the train depot at GCSR. We were told that cabs would be readily available but on Saturday at peak time, only 3 cabs were running at one time. For the volume of visitors this seems destined for disaster. As the entire cab (and it's really a mini-bus) operation is operated by Xanterra there are no alternative options.

We highly recommend the Canyon Spirit Tour on Maverick helicopters. It gave us a fresh experience of the canyon. However, I would make sure you book either a package or have transport arranged for you before you arrive at the park.

"Best hour of my life"--or at least that's how my daughter (not a little kid, but rather a highly accomplished and well travelled professional) described it.  While I trust her exclamation was hyperbolic, I certainly understand her sentiments, even if I don't share her newly acquired ambition to purchase a helicopter.  The Grand Canyon is vast, some 277 miles long.  Short of a couple of weeks on a raft on the Colorado river, or a very very long hike, it is impossible to appreciate fully the majesty and expanse of this natural wonder other than by air.  I'm a confirmed believer in enjoying landscapes slowly and under my own power and don't usually go in for this sort of thing, but the Maverick tour leaving from Tusayan left me breathless and  was worth every penny (and it takes a lot of pennies to fly with Maverick).  Maverick uses aircraft explicitly designed for sightseeing, which means extra glass, stadium seating, all seats facing forward and somewhat less noise and vibration (although you will certainly still need to wear the supplied noise cancelling headphones).  Other companies do not necessarily use these specially purposed copters. Since all companies follow the same route, your choice basically depends on the kind of aircraft they fly and the quality of the pilot.  Our pilot was tremendously knowledgeable, mixed a good deal of information with a bit of humor and made every effort to insure a pleasant and relaxed experience for all.  We happened to have the great good fortune to sit in the front row of seats which undoubtedly offer a superior experience--you can request the front row, but ultimately seating is determined by the need to distribute passenger weight.  We took the longer 45 minute tour (which actually lasted closer to an hour); there isn't much difference in price compared to shorter flights from Tusayan, and I can see no reason why anyone would opt for less time over the canyon, short of a fear of heights in which case they don't belong on this trip anyway.  I won't attempt to describe the sights you will see, since words can not do justice to the undulating otherworldly beauty of this place.  Its as simple as this:  If you are going to the trouble of visiting the Grand Canyon and can afford the fare, take this flight!  Economize if need be on accommodations or meals (you can eat anywhere) and take this flight!  (I've spent 8 years regretting not taking a helicopter over the Na-apali coast on Kauai--avoid my folly!)
Oh, there is one negative:  The staff at the terminal are unhelpful, borderline rude, our flight departed 30 minutes early, we were hustled aboard and were not informed until the last minute that you can't bring pretty much anything aboard other than a camera and a bottle of water, forcing us to make some rather hurried adjustments. (Do bring your camera rather than paying the outrageous fees they will charge you for a video of your flight or a family photo).  Bottom line:  Maverick ain't great on the ground, but once airborne, its a nearly transcendental experience.

review_text:
Halfway through our 45-minute tour, our pilot, BJ, asked us to let him know as soon as he'd made it to the top of our "coolest thing ever done" list. I replied, "You hit that the second we headed over the edge of the canyon!" Truly, that moment 7 minutes into the flight when we shot off the plateau of Kaibab National Forest and the Grand Canyon opened up beneath us is something I'll never forget, not to mention the unbelievable views throughout the rest of the tour.

Maverick Helicopters offers several tours in Nevada and Arizona, and reviews of different ones are combined here on TA; make sure to focus on the reviews for the specific tour you're considering taking. My review applies only to the Canyon Spirit Helicopter Tour, which departs from the South Rim Helicopter Terminal, about 6 miles south of the Grand Canyon National Park entrance, perfect for people driving themselves. 

BJ was the ideal pilot: wicked sense of humour, very proactive about sharing interesting facts about the geology of the canyon, and able to answer every question thrown at him. I noted that he was also simply amazing at taking away the nervousness of the two little girls who, along with their dad, had the front seats, and he kept them engaged with jokes and questions throughout the flight.

My father and I were fortunate to each get window seats in the back row. A window seat is a must if you plan to take decent photos (a major goal for me) as you need to put your camera right against the glass to avoid reflections. Anyone stuck in a middle rear seat would not only miss photo ops but also have quite a restricted view. Currently, Maverick offers no way to reserve a specific seat position in advance, so you pays your money and you takes your chance. Since many of the negative reviews on TA reflect unhappiness with seat assignments, I'll bet that Maverick would find plenty of takers for special flights with reduced passenger numbers that avoid the need to stick anyone in a rear middle seat—I'd certainly have paid a lot more for that guarantee. This would still allow the pilot to assign the prime seating as needed to balance weight.

Be aware too that the pilots play music throughout the flight, and since musical tastes differ, you may not be keen on their choice. I wasn't (hard rock's not my scene), but honestly the Grand Canyon was so mind-blowing that BJ could have played an album of Inuit throat singing and I probably wouldn't have minded. I'll bet you find the same.

As mementos, you can purchase a photo of yourself with the pilot taken by a Maverick staff member at the start of the flight, and a DVD of your specific tour taken by the video camera mounted underneath the chopper, which includes the audio of all cockpit conversations and the background music. You are free to take photos to your heart's content during the flight (don't forget to pack extra memory cards), but not on the ground on the helipad, for legitimate safety reasons.

Check-in was quick and friendly. They need to weigh you for weight distribution on the chopper, but this is painless as the scale is built into the floor at the check-in desk; don't worry if you're not proud of your stats, as they don't broadcast your number to the room or even mention it to you. Note that you're not allowed to bring a backpack or handbag on board, so plan accordingly. I had my camera on a shoulder strap, and that was no problem.

My 80-year-old dad was grinning ear-to-ear throughout the flight, and hasn't stopped raving about it since. This tour is absolutely worth the $274 per person charge; I give it my highest recommendation. Heartfelt thanks to BJ and the Maverick ground crew for a priceless memory.

The flight over the Grand Canyon is one of the most amazing things I have ever done and it something that I will remember for a very long time. It is ABSOLUTLEY BRILLIANT and I would highly recommend it to anyone. If there were a list of things that you simply must do before you die, this would have to be somewhere in the top ten. Seeing the Grand Canyon from the air enables you to appreciate it in a way which is just not possible from the ground. The pilot was extremely friendly and enthusiastic, ensuring that all the passengers were eager and excited before we have even taken off,  and his commentary and overall professionalism during the flight made the experience all the more enjoyable.

I took my flight from Maverick Helicopter’s base at Grand Canyon Airport, near Tusayan. They offer a pleasant waiting area and sell refreshments, t-shirts and souvenirs. The flight itself is recorded, and you have the option afterwards of buying a souvenir DVD of your own actual flight, together with a photograph of yourself standing next to the helicopter before take-off.

If you have previously taken a helicopter ride over a city, it is possible that you may have thought that it was good but not great, or that it was a lot of money to pay for quite a short experience and perhaps not worth the cost. If this is the case, do not let that put you off. Having also taken helicopter rides over cities, I can say that the Grand Canyon experience is in a completely different league, and whilst on a city flight you may get only around 15 or 20 minutes, here you get a good 40 minutes or more in the air. 

The flight currently costs $275 per person (plus tip, plus cost of souvenir photo, DVD, T-shirt etc.!) A common response I had in the days immediately afterwards when raving about the trip to other people and trying to persuade them to do it was “But it is very expensive”.  It is of course perfectly reasonable that any rational person will be apprehensive about spending such a large amount of money and question whether it is wise.

When it comes to this experience, my advice is this: Don’t dwell on it; if you possibly can, say to yourself ‘never mind the cost’, and just do it. Whether this is your first time in a helicopter or you have flown in one many times before, you are in for an amazing time and you will not regret it.

We found several great options, but ended up going with K2 Aviation since their availability best matched our schedule. We chose the Denali Flyer Tour because we wanted to see multiple sides of Denali but didn't think the Grand Denali was quite worth the added cost.

We arrived really early since the drive from Denali to Talkeetna took less time than we anticipated. We hung out in the parking lot and on the picnic benches in front of K2. They provide water, tea, etc.There was also WiFi for guests but it didn't work for me.

We checked in 30-45 minutes before our flight. Each person weights themselves with everything they're taking onto the plane. You can also borrow sunglasses at this time if you need. They have a great selection with all sorts of styles and sizes. We also got our overboots at this time.

About 10 minutes before our flight, the pilot called us over and gave us a safety briefing. Then, we got on the plane. He took volunteers for co-pilot and everyone else sat wherever they wanted. Every seat has a headset and a window. The headset is a bit uncomfortable since it really closes in on your ears and head.

The flight itself was incredible! We flew over the park and soared through the mountains. Our pilot pointed out all the major landmarks from the summits to glaciers. He didn't provide much information besides that, which was fine with me. He did a good job of showing Denali to both sides of the plane so everyone was able to get photos. 

Near the end of the flight, we landed on Ruth Glacier. It was more like a field of snow than glacier ice, which was a little disappointing, but still a beautiful place. We had about 15 minutes on the glacier and then we got back on the plane and headed back.

Oh! One thing to note, it was rather hot when we were in Denali (highs of 75-80). It was also warm on the glacier and basically everyone wore short sleeves and jeans or shorts. No gloves, beanies, jackets, etc. were necessary.

Overall, I would recommend the flight to folks considering it. I wouldn't say it was the highlight of my trip, but it was definitely up there!

On the way back, he managed to catch sight of the very peak of Mt. Denali which had cleared for a few moments and we could see the top!  

A few people in our crew felt a little nauseous during the flight.  If this happens to you, I recommend removing the headset. We love K2 and are looking forward to coming back to Talkeetna again to hopefully get in the Grand Denali Tour w/ glacier landing next time!

We were not bothered by the rescheduling and found lots to do in Talkeetna to kill the time.  When we returned in the afternoon, the sales clerk told us that we could not land on the glacier due to weather conditions, but that we could see the "Matanuska Glacier." Once in the air, however, we learned for the first time that the Matanuska Glacier was not even part of Denali National Park!  Instead, we made a heading towards Anchorage.  Had we been told that the Matanuska Glacier was not part of DNP, we would have rebooked for another day when we could have seen the park from the air! In summary, this was a very expensive excursion and lacked the "bang for the buck."

Will, our pilot, was great in explaining where we were, what we were seeing and in flying the plane.  Our flight was so smooth, I was never scared.  It lasted a little over an hour.  I highly recommend doing this, you will not regret it.  Well worth the money.

My husband and I signed up for this flight seeing tour as part of our Alaskan tour/cruise vacation. It was recommended by others and the price was reasonable.
Pros: Clean, well maintained aircraft. Professional pilots and ground crew. Established flight routes offering unparalleled sights of some of the most remote areas in Denali National Park and Alaska Range. Flexibility to adjust tour based on constantly changing weather conditions (see cons). Well supplied gift shop with reasonably priced offerings of hats, shirts, pullovers, videos and patches/stickers. K2 offered us a refund for the flight we were unable to complete. They also offered an alternate tour operating at lower altitudes, refunding the difference from the original tour. We accepted the latter. 
Regardless of tour selected, it is difficult to imagine not having a phenomenal time. We really enjoyed the glacier tour since the Denali Flyer was cancelled due to bad weather up near the summit.
Cons: Constantly changing weather conditions may make your desired flight tour unavailable at times.
Small office/waiting room/gift shop. It’s Alaska, so Mosquitos...

Took a flight to land on the Ruth Glacier. It was absolutely BREATHTAKING. Our pilot Mike pointed out the landscape as he flew and helped ease my mind as I was admittedly a little nervous about flying in a small plane over the mountains! But it was amazing. Who can say they landed on a glacier?!? We can! My 14 year old daughter had a blast as Mike let her ride in the co-pilot seat on the way out. Highly recommend this company if you are in the Denali area and want to see beauty!!!!

We were very lucky that when we traveled to Denali we had clear sky's and a great view of the mountain.  Our reservation was for another day, but we called and the K2 staff were flexible to get us up early to see the mountain given the clear sky's.  Our pilot, Jason was great!  There are other aviation companies, but you will not be disappointed with K2! I even purchased a hoodie that I wore the entire trip to Alaska!

When we arrived at K2 we were disappointed to learn that because of low cloud and changeable weather conditions we would not be able to land on the glacier. We were given a range of options and decided to go on the Denali Flyer.
 It was the best decision we have made as the flight under pilot Randy was the smoothest ever and his expert skills enabled us to see all the major glaciers while flying above and below cloud and what seemed right next to sheer cliff faces. We even caught views of the mighty Mount Denali.

review_text:
This was a great experience from start to finish, starting with quick responses to initial enquiries, preflight contacts and information, safety briefing and the engagement of an experienced pilot with us all constantly explaining the scenic area and easing any concerns we may have had as we flew over the most daunting and majestic mountains and glaciers. 
The planes were very clean and well maintained, very powerful and ideal for the type of work expected of them to fly in mountain terrain.  Windows were very clean enabling surprisingly good photography.
The history of the area was well explained as we flew. Although we did not manage a glacial landing due to cloud conditions, the whole experience was exceptional.It would be one of the best experiences we had in our 3 weeks in Alaska. April, often seen as not a good time to be in Alaska due to the melting snow, actually was really good as the day light hours are long, the landscape is still well covered in snow, the lakes and rivers are largely still iced over, but thawing and there were no mosquitos yet to worry about!
Great experience and very much recommend.

In May, I took the opportunity to take a flight up into the Alaska Range with K2 Aviation.  Wow!  We have some of the best pilots in the world here in Alaska and Barry (our pilot) surely didn’t disappoint us. These pilots here are consummate pros.  Words don’t do these flights justice, the way even great photographs don’t do Alaska justice.  About the best description I can think of is that you will NEVER forget the visual overload and truly  awesome views on the enjoyable (understated) flight.  This is a Must Do on your trip to Alaska. Again, a flight you won’t soon forget!!!

We booked this nearly a year in advance for 5 of us.  The pilot was top notch and the views were amazing.  My little one (very use to flying) had some ear issues and he tried his best to alleviate them on our decent.  I was a bit disappointed because we weren't able to land; however being safe is most important.  The one thing that I didn't like is that we rode with another family who made sure they got right in the front and when the pilot announced that someone could sit in the co-pilot seat, I spoke up stating that my husband would really love to do that, yet the man in the other family went straight up there and sat down- HOW RUDE!  Their child also kept looking back at my daughter who was having ear issues.  I don't know when they booked, but perhaps they should have some sort of policy based on when you book as to who gets to do something special like that, or, if it is safe, let one person do it going up and another going back down.  I felt really bad for my husband and wanted to tell the other people off, but of course, would never do so in front of my daughter.

To be able to see and understand how big Alaska is, you need to go on a flightseeing tour. Up in the air you realize truly how small you are in this world and how Denali Park area’s landscape was formed is much better understood from the air. We were in a 1950s Havilland plane, total of 8 passengers. We all had headsets and our pilot gave us a nice overview of Talkeetna, Denali Park, how the Alaska Range and glaciers came to be, etc. Although we couldn’t see Denali or land on a glacier it was an awesome opportunity to see mountains and glaciers up close. It was awe inspiring. Do it, go, you won’t regret it. 
By the way, if you forget sunglasses there are some for you to borrow at the check in office. Also, don’t bring anything into the plane besides your camera and sunglasses. They are pretty strict about the quantity and weight of things you bring on board.

We selected K2 for our Denali experience, and have no regrets at all. Chris was a great pilot, shared a lot of interesting information during the flight, and then gave us a smooth landing on Ruth Glacier. Spending time on the glacier was the absolute highlight of our trip and the best experience of my life. Everything about the trip with K2 was perfect. If you want to visit Denali, forget looking anywhere else and just book with K2!!!

I would have appreciated if canceled the flight or told us upfront that we WON'T see snow mountains. When I talked to the lady there she was not responsive. I am sure they have good trips when whether is nice but there is no need to give us trips that are worth it.

We arrived on an overcast day and we could not see Denali from our hotel for the clouds so I was worried it would not be as good as intended. Then we took flight, I saw bald eagles at the top of the trees, the weather cleared and we followed the river/glacier up to Denali. Unlike anything we have ever experienced. My wife and son saw grizzly bears and we all were treated to great views of the glacier and Denali's peak. The whole time the ride was smooth and enjoyable!  Awesome!

Amazing flight to mount Denali. There were some bad weather conditions so we could not do the flight we had previously booked but K2 made its best to rebook us in another flight.

Seeing Denali and the glaciers from their plane was unbelievable.  Just the majesty of nature up close is so humbling. review_text:
The mountains and glaciers are  everywhere in Alaska and beautiful to see, but there is nothing like seeing  them out the window of a 9 seater bush plane! Amazing!
K2 aviation offers different flying experiences. Very safety conscious and reputable, pilots are excellent. We had a flight booked to land on a glacier, but did a fly around the mountains and glaciers only, as they felt the mountain was too unstable to land.  They adjust the price of your flight if changes, to your original tour, are made. They are also happy to give a full refund if you prefer. K2 keeps in touch through email the evening before and morning of your flight, with weather and flight updates. Washrooms available before your flight. Everyone is weighed before flight and  backpacks etc are locked in a container to be picked up once your flight is finished. Of course take your camera! The pilot takes pictures of you and your group with the plane you fly in. K2 is close and an easy walk  from the main street in Talkeetna, but they also offer a shuttle. 
An expensive tour, but well worth it!

found_pos_words: amazed, comfortable, confident, glad, stunning, talented
review_text:
I went on the glacier landing flight without hubby who had no desire to be in a small plane.  From the minute I met Chip, our pilot, to the minute we landed at the Talkeetna Airport I was truly amazed and was SO glad I did this!

The take off and landing at the glacier are as smooth as can be.  The views were stunning and indescribable. The whole experience makes me believe in God even more - how can such beauty exist in this world ?  

The plane is small but comfortable. There are headphones so you can hear the pilot narrate what you're seeing as you go, and you can ask questions along the way.  Chip was the quintessential Alaskan pilot  - young, handsome, confident  and a very talented pilot. Never felt uneasy once.  

If there's one thing that will stand out in my 15 days in Alaska this is it - wouldn't have missed it for the world!!

review_text:
We were lucky to have reserved on the single sunny day of our two weeks vacation and it was the best day of our trip.
As the weather was great and we had come in early, they accommodated us with an earlier flight with another couple in a four passenger Cessna with a great pilot whose name I am sorry to have forgotten ( see the picture).
Our pilot had a constant interesting commentary and was able to answer all our questions. He flew us so close to the mountain peaks and up and down the glaciers valleys that my pictures turned out great. He made sure that both sides of the plane had great views and such a beautiful sunny day the white of the mountains was blinding. We really got a great view of all the features of the glaciers as well as the plains below. This experience made the price worth it

We did the Denali Flyer flight.  It was an awesome experience.  Our pilot Billy J was excellent and had a wealth of knowledge about Denali/Alaska past and present.  When we arrived, It was fairly overcast in Talkeetna so I was worried about the view from the plane.  K2 told me the viewing would still be good near and around Denali and they were correct!   Take one of K2s flights - you will be glad you did.  Also spend some time in Talkeetna after your flight.

We waited out four days for good weather to fly.  They were great with helping us understand what was going on and rolling our reservations.  Our patience was rewarded with 100% clear day and a trip of a lifetime! Our pilot Chip gave us a wonderful narrated tour (he voice is so soothing!).  We would do this flightseeing experience again in a heartbeat!  Only disappointment was not being able to land on the glacier due to it being too soft (not K2's fault), so some day we want to do this again to have this experience.  Definitely book with K2 Aviation!

My aunt visited and was disappointed The Mountain wasn't showing. I kept this a secret until we arrived in Talkeetna. Although weather had been troublesome, and the glacier landings were stopped due to softer conditions, going up with K2 made viewing Denali possible! The clouds cleared enough around Denali when we arrived to make it possible for her to see the summit. This was thanks to Daniel circling around for us and then getting in above much of the Alaska Range adjacent to Denali. Hunter and Foraker were viewable as well. Thanks so much to K2! I will share with everyone I meet that this is the way to go!

We took the 1 hour glacier view trip. The clouds were low which made it difficult to get near the mountain. We did see one glacier. The pilot noticed a clearing in the cloud cover due west. He took us to the clearing and we ascended to 12000 feet. There we were able to see the tops of Denali and Foraker! We then proceeded back to the visible glacier and flew along it for some spectacular pictures. I believe the pilot went above and beyond to make sure we were satisfied! Good for him and the K2 Aviation company!

Unfortunately Denali was socked in with weather. Also the glaciers had degraded to the point of no landings. We were very sad. K2 offered us an option to Knik. It was UNBELIEVABLE!!!!!  Clear skies and late day sun gave us spectacular views!  Mark was an amazing pilot and guide. Nobody can control Mother Nature but K2 will find you a memorable safe alternative. I highly recommend K2 and Mark!

The price might turn some away, but it is worth it and more the views of mountain range and almost neon blue water and ice if you are in the season fir glacier landings add that you won't be disappointed

We had a great experience with K2 Aviation and our pilot, whose name I unfortunately don't remember.

Had a beautiful day. Mark (our pilot) was extremely knowledgeable. My second flight on K2. My family enjoyed very much.
Had a mix up on flight time, my fault. They worked hard to get us up as soon as possible. Great customer service.

We took this float plane to hike up in Denali National Park.  I'm terrified of small planes but this was too cool to be afraid of!   The flight was amazing!  It was just our four family members and the pilot on a dehavilland beaver plane.   We flew up the Ruth Glacier and saw the Backside Glacier.  We landed on Moraine Lake for a two hour hike. I have always been afraid of small planes, but, after reading so many raving reviews, I decided this was worth it.  And, i never felt any fear during the flight.  The scenery is beyond anything I can describe -- total awesomeness of G-d.  Unfortunately, our glacier landing was cancelled due to weather, but the flight still exceeded my expectations.

We took the long trip, I think it was called the Summit rip that went up and around the summit of Denali. I felt like the only way we could get closer to her would be if we were climbers. I tood the K2 Denali flightseeing and glacier landing flight and it was by far the most exciting trip I have ever taken.  Flying over the Alaskan range and viewing the peaks, crevices, ice, snow, rocks brings one closer to God than you can imagine.  It is a very spiritual flight even if you are not spiritual. Sad to see that a hotel is being built there - it should be left to nature and sleeping in tents if you dare...K2 did a fabulous job with everything for orientation to take off and landings and I would highly recommend taking a K2 adventure if you want the trip of a lifetime.

While we missed our Summit Tour with Glacier Landing due to the weather conditions this company was great to work with - both before our trip and once we arrived.  They kept us informed about the status of the flight and we were so disappointed to miss it.  We will be make and make the highly anticipated flight.

I would just want to summarize our experience in one word "Awesome".   A must do activity, the experience is mind boggling and I bet you will not regret your decision.  Trained staff, courteous and knowledgeable about the place, facts and history.

Unfortunately for us, the weather made it impossible to see Denali or land on a glacier. review_text: You can't go to Alaska and not experience a floatplane trip! Both K-2 and Rust's Flying Service are GREAT! Informative, friendly pilots and staff. They are very honest with people regarding flight conditions and visibility...so you don't have to worry about wasting your money because they won't fly if conditions are not good. Flightseeing can be expensive but it is lots of fun and very scenic...we loved our experience!

Our flight over Denali National Park was wonderful. I was a little fearful of going into a small plane, but it was a 10-seater, driven by Randy. He was excellent!! No fears from me. Seeing the park from above was something I'm glad I didn't skip. If you have the opportunity, just do it. You will never regret it.

I highly recommend K2 aviation for a flight tour of Mt. Denali. I did a lot of research before booking K2 and they did not disappoint me. This was one of the highlights of our trip. We flew from Talkeetna and did the Grand Tour with glacier landing. For starters, the pilot was great and really knew the mountain. Seeing Mt. Denali up close and in the air was well worth the price. It was so cool to land on one of the glaciers in the Alaska range so don't skip out on the landing. We were informed that if weather prevented the glacier landing we would be refunded that amount of money, but luckily didn't need it as the clouds moved out of the way just in time. As our flight was at 11:00am, I wouldn't recommend earlier as the morning clouds may limit the landing and view of the mountain.

I had a "reservation" to fly, but waited over a hour. I saw lightening and storm clouds- I was told by pilot that it was a small cell that we'd fly around. IMMEDIATELY after takeoff the pilot said there were forest fires north of us and there was a bad haze decreasing visibility, and the increasing cloud cover would not allow us to see Denali!! The pilot played music and rarely spoke! When he did it was impossible to decifer what he said. When we landed on the glacier, he told us he liked flying, but was an introvert and hated talking! Then why was he doing flightseeing?? I'd done this flight previously and loved it- this one not so much! I know there are no guarantees, but K2 KNEW  the visibility was poor! I'm in Denali now- friends are supposed to fly today with another company, that has postponed the flight due to poor visibility and will cancel if it doesn't clear! Now that's how it should be done! Not just grab the money!! Check visibility/ ask people getting back what they saw. Expensive lesson!!

The rule of thumb is that there is a 1 in 3 chance of seeing Denali (Mt. McKinley) without cloud cover. However, on those days that Denali is in the open a flight is a must if your budget can manage it.

One morning following a rainy day we saw that Denali was in view and immediately booked a flight with K2 Aviation, which has a menu of several flight options including landing and walking on a glacier, flying over the lower reaches of the mountain, or flying over and around the  entire mountain. We chose the least expensive flight, over the lower reaches of the mountain, because it was the least expensive, my wife is nervous about flying in small planes, and I saw that lenticular clouds were starting to form near the mountain, a sign of high winds and turbulence.

The booking over the phone went fairly quickly; the drive to K2 took about an hour. There was a bit of a wait for processing, and so many people had booked flights that  there was little room indoors to sit until departing on our six-passenger Piper Cherokee, which was small but comfortable in terms of seating space and cabin temperature. 

We had a capable and well-informed pilot who provided an ongoing narrative that covered the key points of the area and Denali; he also kept a sharp eye out for moose (we spotted several) and bear (no luck). It turned out that high winds cut short the trips of the planes slated to fly above and around the entire mountain, so we were glad we had not opted for that.

We could hear our pilot talking to the control tower from time to time throughout the flight, reporting our location at various key points along the way and keeping track of the numerous other planes in our vicinity (when Denali is visible, all the flight tour services in the area are heavily booked). It is clear that K2's safety protocol is rigorous and well-execute.

Bottom line:  A wonderful experience, would do it again, many thanks to K2.

After spending $400 round trip to get to K2, we were told that our glacier walk / plane tour was cancelled when we got there. Why they could not tell us earlier was disappointing. There wasn't a lot to do in the town where they are located and we were stuck until our arranged transportation left. It was too late to book anything else. I get the weather can cancel flights; however, maybe be nicer about it and offer something more than a refund? To add insult to injury, while we were having dinner, we saw one of their planes that had the landing gear for ice pass over us.

The clouds parted as we approached Denali and my jaw dropped. The glorious twin peaks came into view veiled with misty clouds and the sun drenched snow covered shear walls of granite blew my mind. We circle heaven for 30 minutes and then dropped down to follow Ruth glacier all the way back home. 

This was my second trip to Talkeetna. The first time it rained and I never saw the mountain so this time I allowed three days to stay flexible with flying times. Sure enough it rained on our scheduled flight time but K2 was very good about rescheduling for the next day and even suggested I call before my flight time to see if there was and opening for our group to land on the glacier.
