review_text:
Beautiful flight, confused office staff and dishonest pilot took away from what could've been an amazing experience!  Doing a land tour on our own prior to a cruise, we decided we would include a sightseeing tour if time and weather permitted.  The day we left Denali NP I called K2 Aviation and was told we were doing flights and they would need to have me in the office at minimum 30 minutes prior to flight.  We planned a hike in Denali so decided to call after we left Denali and see if there were still seats available.  After we were on the road for a bit and I got a cell tower signal I called K2 Aviation.  I was told there was seats available to accommodate our family of 4 and I could either book it over the phone or just wait until we arrived.  We were still about an hour away so I was a bit concerned that the seats may be sold by the time we got there.  I was assured that was unlikely as it was an empty plane and they could do whatever tour we wanted.  I was told there were two flights we could choose either 6:30pm or 7:00pm.  I told the lady on the phone that it would be after 6pm so we would probably have to take the 7pm flight since she also said we would have to be in the office 30 minutes prior to our flight.  Since my cell service was not very good and getting worse I told her we would wait until we got there, as she had suggested, to reserve with our names.  We rushed to get there omitting a few stops/pullouts along the way (boo, as Denali was out in plain view).  

We get to the office and are inside by 6:20pm only to be told they weren't sure there were enough seats for us and the flight was at 6:30.  I told them I was told over the phone that there was another flight at 7pm.  The girl said that flight was moved up to 6:30 to accommodate guests who had to be back for a  "Princess" tour departure.  She said she would ask the dispatcher.  As I was waiting another person came up and asked if they could help.  I explained the other girl was checking on the flight.  Eventually one of them came back and said they could take us on the 6:30 flight.  I said that's only in 10 minutes, is there time?  She said she would check and then I was told there was actually two flights, but they were both at 6:30.  Then another person told me one would leave after the other and that there was indeed one at 7pm, but that all flights actually had to be in the air by 7pm.  We wanted the Denali summit with glacier landing since we had been told over the phone they could do any flight we wanted.  However, the girl said both flights were the Denali Experience flights.  I doubt we would have rushed there skipping pullouts/viewpoints with fabulous views of Denali for that flight, but since we were already there we decided to take that flight.  I said I would take the last flight as it would give us more time to fill out paperwork, go to the restroom, and it would not be rushed to get back due to the "Princess" tour people.  So while we were waiting we looked around at shirts and my husband asked the girl if the office would be open for us to buy shirts when we got back.  She said yes, so we proceeded outside to wait for our flight.

We all were excited and my son especially was excited.  He was first in line standing at the gate with my husband while everyone else sat in chairs and waited.  When the pilot came through he even made comment to my son and husband that they were ready to go waiting at the gate.  As we ventured out to the plane, the pilot went over some standard safety rules, etc.  Then he asked if anyone would like to be his "co-pilot".  My son raised his hand and another girl (not sure of age probably around 14-17) raised hers.  He told the girl to climb in and looked at my son and said we will switch when we land on the glacier that there would actually be two opportunities to "co-pilot".  Since we were at the front of the line we moved to the front seats of the plane so others would not have to be climbing around as they entered and were seated.  I didn't think much about it, but our seats had to be some of the worst.  I was second row and could not get a clear view for a photo without part of the plane in the photograph.  It wasn't great, but it was still beautiful  The weather was beautiful and the landscape is amazing!  We had a great flight and landing on the glacier.  Other planes were there and we were the last to leave since we were the last flight.  So at one point we were the only plane on the glacier, which was nice.  However, as we were getting ready to get back into the plane I overheard the pilot tell a woman to climb on up in the seat beside him.  I stopped and turned around and said I thought (I said my son's name) was going to get to co-pilot on the return.  The pilot kind of hemmed around and said well, you can't really see from there anyway.  I said well, I understood he would get that chance on the way back and he was looking forward to it.  The pilot looked at my 13 y/o son (who is small for his age) and said well you can't really see anything from there anyway.  He continued to say all of the controls would block his view from the front.  I said well he was looking forward to it.  The pilot told the lady to go ahead.  Needless to say my son was crushed!  My son is a bit reserved and doesn't speak up for himself much so he remained quiet, but I could see the look on his face he was obviously disappointed.  The pilot had basically told him he could co-pilot on the return, but then gave that opportunity to someone else.  The part that made my husband most upset was the fact that the pilot was condescending by saying the control panel would make it harder for him to see!  Actually there is a wall between the 1st row and the pilot cockpit area.  So the only view from the seat we were in was from the side window anyway!  The co-pilot still would have the side window to see out of!  So no, Mr. Pilot, that was a lie!  The view would not have been worse from the co-pilot seat!  

So when we landed he turned around and told my son that after he parked he could climb into the co-pilot seat and see what it was like if he wanted!  Seriously?!  When the plane came to a stop the lady in the co-pilot seat handed the pilot a tip.  I sure hope he got what he deserved from that tip, because he lost the $50 tip from us!  There were four of us (also have a 12 y/o daughter) so our plan was to tip $50.  When we exited the plane I asked my husband if he was going to stop by the office to get the shirts we picked out.  He said "nah, I don't want any".  He then looked at my son and asked if he wanted a shirt (we had all picked out shirts), but my son just shook his head no.  He was obviously crushed.  So we headed straight for the car and left.  After we left I reminded my husband I had wanted to purchase the video of our flight, but forgot because I was so upset over what had happened.  I honestly don't remember much about the return flight as I was so upset and disappointed for my son that I was distracted.  

I want to emphasize that it's not that I expect my son to have had the opportunity over anyone else, but it was the fact that the pilot and told him he could have that opportunity on the return flight and then gave it to someone else.  Then the pilot told my son he wouldn't be able see over the controls anyway.  Horrible!   My daughter is 12 y/o and the only reason she didn't raise her hand to co-pilot was because she knew it meant a lot to her brother and she wanted him to have that opportunity.  

So, why two stars?  I believe the experience could have been amazing!  The planes seem to be good condition, but I can't vouch for sure.  I deducted for the miscommunication from the office staff over the phone vs. when we got there.  Not to mention that I was getting different info from different people even after I was physically in the office.  Finally, the dishonesty of the pilot.  I believe a company is only as good as the people who work there.  So a confusing office staff and dishonest pilot takes away 3 stars!  I wish we had taken our time driving and experienced the beautiful scenery along our drive and skipped this tour.  I'd rather have not had the experience than to see my son treated so poorly!  With such beautiful landscape, this should have been nothing short of an amazing experience!

Oh, and I want to mention that although we were the last flight and the last to leave the glacier, our pilot had to slow down as he had caught up with the plane that left several minutes before us.  Apparently some of the Princess people were also on our plane and he was rushing to get them back!  So we landed right behind the other plane.  

Now to help those who plan to take this tour anyway here are the tips I'd offer:

Bring:  Camera, a jacket (wasn't terribly cold on the glacier), sunglasses, and extra cash for gratuities in the event you have a great experience and wish to tip the pilot.  

Make advance reservations and don't rely on the info given over the phone to wait until you get there.

If you have a glacier landing flight they have complimentary glacier boots that fit over your shoes prior to you taking the flight.  

Most importantly have no expectations!

review_text: I am not afraid of flying but I have a fear of heights, which usually means commercial flight is OK but small aircraft flight is white knuckle.  We flew up to Denali in a DeHavilland Beaver that was two years younger than I am but meticulously maintained and flown beautifully.  Admittedly, my knuckles were white for 15 minutes, but the pilot's skill and the overall stability of the trip won me over and I greatly enjoyed my time in the air.  I would definitely do it again.  If you are an aviation buff, you will enjoy the ride in the Beaver.  A ride in the DeHavilland is like a ride on a Harley... not the fastest ride out there but it has a quality that is classic and as memorable as the scenery.  Make sure you take your earphones off for a bit while in flight to hear and feel the deep rumble only a radial piston engine can give you.  The pilot's narration was packed with great information that was interesting and well researched (unlike the mind numbing prattle of most Alaskan tour bus drivers who drone on for hours about their own idiotic reflections on life).  The views were beyond wonderful... transcendent, if you are lucky enough to have a clear day.  You will want to take stills and videos, so clear up your SDS camera card!  One other note, I noticed that the pilot was in constant communication with ground control and the other pilots in the air with us, regularly exchanging positions and headings. review_text: We traveled to Talkeetna, Alaska late this summer with the sole mission of completing the glacier landing on Denali.  Our trip last year was foiled by rain every day.  When we arrived, there was not a cloud in sight, so we immediately traveled to K2 Aviation in order to take full advantage of the beautiful weather. What a pleasant surprise.  We were greeted by K2 personnel and the trip was outlined and priced for us and we immediately booked a flight within just a few minutes.  All aspects of the flight were explained and our questions answered thoroughly and completely.  We were soon introduced to our pilot, Patrick.  What a surprise to discover that he was from our home state.  With just a few pre-flight instructions, we were off to the wild blue yonder.  The scenery was absolutely breath-taking.  The glacier landing was smooth and awesome.  Our pilot got so close to the mountain on the flight over that it seemed that you could reach out and touch the mountain. review_text:
We only had two precious days to spend in Talkeetna and when we left Anchorage to drive up it was totally cloudy and raining. It proceeded to rain for the next 30 hours so we were worried about seeing Denali. We called to inquire about a Flightseeing trip with k2 and they helped us book for a 6:30 flight with a backup the next day. I got the impression right away that they really wanted us to have the best experience possible - it was so different than a helicopter ride in Hawaii where when you book, you're completely locked in no matter the weather or what happens. Here, I got a sense there was flexibility to accommodate the client (go figure, huh?!). We stopped in around 2 to check on things - it was still looking cloudy but they said things were improving and to check back around 6 (for our 6:30 flight). We showed up close to 6 and agonized about what to do - there are no guarantees and things can change so rapidly. The staff were so helpful and were talking to pilots currently at the mountain. Again, at the last minute, we had the option to reschedule (without penalty) for the next day!  We decided to go for it, knowing we'd probably not see Denali but would see the area and the park. 

Our pilot was Michael - he's quiet with a great sense of humor and wit!  He really worked FOR us and was very knowledgable about the area!  He was literally turning from Denali because of the clouds when he saw a last minute opening, turned around back towards Denali, and found every opening he could to see the mountain. It was really everything and more we had hoped for!  He even spied a moose (one for each side of the plane) on the return back to Talkeetna. 

I would highly recommend - it was the highlight of our trip!

I think these people try hard, but Denali is often under cloud cover as she was the day we visited.  It was unfortunate but our guide offered us a two hour ride looking at some other glaciers, lakes, etc., in another direction for a lesser place.  We had a good time and saw a lot of beautiful country and even some wildlife from the plane!  I was very disappointed we couldn't do the original tour to see Denali and have a glacier landing, but then man cannot control the weather!  Thanks!

I took the 90-minute excursion with my sister and wife, and we had an amazing time. The planes K2 flies are mostly 11-person aircraft (including the pilot and a seat up front for a passenger), and though I was worried about a bumpy flight, it was anything but. Prior to departure, everyone has the opportunity to put what I would call a boot over their shoes so their feet did not get wet while on the glacier. Our flight took us to Ruth Glacier via a number of turns that brought us within 11 miles of Mt. McKinley (now called Denali) and several other high peaks before landing on Ruth Glacier. After about 15 minutes on the glacier, it was back to Talkeetna. On both legs, our pilot kept us informed via headphones (which are provided on the aircraft) of the altitude and geology of the region. 

TIP: Try to get a seat near the front or the back of the plane. Those sitting in the middle may find that the arm securing the wing to the fuselage will partially obstruct some views. That said, even if sitting in the middle (as I did) will not detract much from what is an amazing sightseeing opportunity.

review_text:
Pre-booked on our Princess Cruisetour, we went for the Denali summit flightseeing tour with K2 Aviation, located at the airport in Talkeetna. A shuttle bus goes from the Princess Lodge to Talkeetna on the hour, and from Talkeetna to the lodge on the ½ hour. We took the shuttle to K2, where we checked in and then were weighed (for weight distribution in the plane), with all clothes, camera, etc. you were taking with you. The plane was a Piper Navajo Chieftain with an unpressurized cabin. Our group had 8 passengers. The pilot gave us an extensive safety talk, including testing the oxygen masks we’d be using over 12,000 ft., and what to do in case we get stranded—an unlikely but real possibility up the mountain. 
		
We took off from Talkeetna, across the flats, between there & the mountain. As we neared the mountain, the view got more and more awesome by the minute. We also had on a headset and microphone so that we could talk and hear the driver and each other (very noisy propeller engines), and a snug seatbelt. The plane is equipped with big nice windows for viewing and picture taking. Everyone has a great view. While circling the mountain, the pilot said that we were within ½ mile of the rock faces and summit. It felt like you could reach your hand out and touch it. It was breathtaking, fantastic, and beyond words to describe. We were able to see several very long glaciers, the summit of the mountain, and the surrounding mountains. From the distance, you have no idea how much detail—valleys, crags, rock, etc. nor how immense and vast the mountain is. There is an unimaginable amount of ice, snow and rock up there. We were able to see where the base camps are for the mountain climbers. I took dozens of pictures trying to take it all in. 

K2 also has flights that land on a glacier, but do not go to the summit. The passengers are outfitted with appropriate gear. Those planes fly at a much lower altitude.

I had some trouble with the altitude, but the others in the group did fine. The pilot and other people at K2 very diligently made sure I was OK before letting us leave for the shuttle back to the hotel. If you have heart or respiratory issues, you may want to check with your doc before doing this tour, just in case. All in all this was an amazing experience, and I would do it again if I had the chance.

review_text:
We visited Alaska in August with another couple. Each person picked one thing they really wanted to do and mine was to see Denali by air. K2 had the best web site and offered different types of flights. I decided on the summit trip. My wife was a bit nervous about flying on such a small plane and having to breathe through a mask, but was willing to go. We prepaid to reserve the flight and I was really looking forward to it.
On the day of our flight, we got to Talkeetna early and stopped by to see the facility early. The three people I was flying with were all happy by how professional and well maintained everything looked. When we checked in later for the flight we were told we couldn't do the summit trip because of the weather. The person at the desk was apologetic and offered us a different trip that they could do. We were okay with that and she took care of everything very swiftly and refunded us the difference in the trip price. If you travel to Alaska, be prepared for this......weather changes quickly and plans may have to change.
The flight was fantastic. There are no words to describe how beautiful and majestic Denali is. The pilot was very knowledgeable and personable and told us what we were looking at all the time. He also told us that he was avoiding snow storms on the mountain and that due to it's size, Denali produces it's own weather. He and the other pilots were talking to each other about the weather conditions throughout the trip.
My apprehensive co-fliers soon forgot they were in a small plane and were as taken in by what we were seeing as I was. The four of us wound up taking over 400 pictures all together. It was the trip of a lifetime for all of us.
If you want a professional and knowledgeable company that does things the right way, then K2 is the way to go.
Jim

review_text:
Talkeetna airfield is situated on the right hand side of the road, just before you enter town. As there is only one way into town, you have to pass it. It is a base for a number of operators offering flight sightseeing tours of Mt McKinley and the area. All the operators offer similar packages and prices for the various trips.

We chose K2 Aviation, having flown with Rusts Flying Services in Anchorage on a bear watching trip. K2 is a sister company to Rusts.

In high season it is probably best to book in advance to avoid disappointment. Though this has to be weighed up with the possibility of the weather not being too good.

We arrived at about 4PM on a Sunday and booked for a 7PM departure that evening. We opted for the 90 minute flight and glacier landing. We were not disappointed.

One of the attractions of K2 and some of the other operators are in the type of aircraft they use on the flights. A good number are on De Havilland DHc2 Beavers and DHc3 Otters. Some of these aircraft are around 50 years old and the type is still very common for bush flying in Alaska. This bit of aviation history often goes unnoticed by passengers and is something that should be a selling point. The operators don’t seem to make a big thing of it. (Or maybe passengers will be put off by the age?)

Our flight was on a six seater DHc2 Beaver N121KT, built in 1958. One passenger usually gets to sit up at the front with the pilot. A good safety demo was given prior to boarding. It was also pointed out to us that the aircraft carried overnight supplies etc, in the extreme case the weather turned and we couldn’t return!

The flight was excellent. Real close up views of the glacier, mountains etc. Stunning scenery. All passengers get a window seat.  On the Beaver, the rear seats are better than the middle as you don’t have a wing strut in front of you. The view from the middle is still excellent, but photos may get the odd strut in them. After landing you are allowed off the aircraft, as long as you keep nearby. The peace and tranquillity is only shattered for a moment when another aircraft lands or takes off. The evening we went it was a clear blue sky – perfect We had around 25 mins on the snow, watching a couple of other flights land and take off (tip – don’t stand downwind of one when it takes off, unless you want to experience a blizzard!)

The return flight is quicker and comes straight back to the airfield, as most of the sightseeing is done on the way up.

If you get the right weather, this trip will be one of the highlights, if not the highlight of your stay.

You may not want to spend five hours in Talkeetna unless you had another tour planned.  It's a small town and there isn't that much to see or do unless you're hiking or taking a tour. Upon arriving in Talkeetna, the day before our flight with my wife, 83 year old father in law, and his 79 year old friend , I stopped into the K2 office to confirm our appointment and pick up. The weather was very rainy with a forecast for more rain and high wind on our flight day. They assure me all was confirmed and that they would pick us up half an hour before our scheduled time to fly.
When leaving Talkeetna by Princess bus to our accommodations ,I discovered we were staying about an hour away from K2, and became concerned about our pick up time for our flight the next morning.  I again contacted K2 again to confirm a time.  This time I mention my concern for the timing of their pickup and my distance away from them.
This time, however , K2 told me they only do pick ups within ten minutes of their facility and it was my responsibility to get all four people to their office by eight am.  
I asked for k2 to call us to let us know if the flight would occur to save us the expense ($10 each) and hassle of a early morning hour long shuttle ride.  They said we needed to physically be in their facility by 8 am....and we're unwavering .
  My understanding was that if we did not show our fee would be forfit regardless of the weather.

When we all showed up at 8 am , in pouring rain, they canceled our epic flight and offered a flight of the town instead , at the same price.  We were not interested in this and so they refunded our fee.  The atmosphere in the office was sullen and quite.

I'm a fairly easy going person but non the less found the staff at K2 to be unfriendly , unhelpful, and unconcerned with 
My needs as a customer.  We talked to friends in our tour group who had booked with other groups and had much clearer and better service.  
After our canceled flight we went to the Roadhouse for breakfast and coffee to warm our bones and were thrilled by the friendly staff there.

We flew with K2 on August 18th.  We were scheduled to circle the mountain and land on a glacier.  Although the weather in Talkeetna was nice, the mountain was surrounded with low clouds, eliminating the glacier landing and the views of surrounding peaks, valleys, and glaciers.  On their suggestion (with no pressure) we opted to fly south and that was a great choice!  Our pilot (Mike) was great and the scenery just spectacular.  Someday we will return to fly around Mt McKinely with K2, but the memories and photos from this first trip are amazing!  Thanks K2 for a great experience! This is a well run operation that really cares about their customers and works hard to give everyone an amazing adventure!

We really lucked out on the day we had planned to go flightseeing to Mt. McKinley with K-2 Aviation.  It was beautiful with sunshine and blue sky. The K-2 shuttle picked us up at our lodge and took us to the airport. They checked us in and we waited on the deck until our pilot came to get us. Remember how they asked your weight when you made your reservations for this? Well, they weigh you again when you get there and you have to hold everything you plan to take with you-like cameras or coats. There is a locked bin for folks to leave backpacks and so forth.  Our pilot was Tony and 3 other couples went with us. Tony did a great job of telling us about the flight and then of taking us up-very smooth-and telling us what we were seeing.  Words or my pictures do not do justice to what actually happened. It was the trip of a lifetime! It was not scary-it was awesome. Don't miss a chance to do this. And BTW, should I go back to Alaska again, I will do the glacier landing!

We decided last minute to do a flightseeing tour, and I'm so glad we flew with K2. We chose the glacier landing, which I highly recommend. Our pilot (Mike) was great. I was nervous to be on such a small plane, but I felt very safe and relaxed the whole time. The views were breathtaking, and I will never forget the feeling of stepping foot on a glacier, surrounded by snow and mountains.

review_text:
Departed the McKinley Lodge @ 7:00 AM for the best breakfast @ the Roadhouse Cafe in
Talkeetna before walking over to K2 Aviation for the best excursion of our Alaskan vacation.
We had booked this tour online months before our arrival.  To our surprise we were offered
a float plane ride which took off from nearby Fish Lake (away from the airport) and carried only
six passengers plus the pilot.  Jeff Babcock was our experienced pilot and guide and he did a terrific job of narrating sights, points of interest, and our location at all times.  If you are the least bit nervous about flying small planes (I am scared of heights), this was safe and comfortable . . . plus the take off and landing was so smooth on the water.  This was our splurge tour of the trip . . . we knew we would never see God's beautiful, awesome creation unless we took to the skies.  It was AMAZING!!!  We flew over Moose Field, the Ruth Glacier,
the Great Gorge, the Don Sheldon Ampitheater, viewed the southern face of Mt. McKinley,
Mt. Foraker, Mt. Hunter, Mt. Silverthrone, Harper Glacier from the top, Kahitna Glacier,
Traleka Glacier, Mt. Dickey and Moose's Tooth before returning to Fish Lake.  We felt like National Geographic Explorers flying over ancient territory!  Don't forget your camera!!
We took this tour on July 24, 2012 and allotted approximately 2.45 hours.
K2 Aviation is welcoming, organized, accommodating, well-staffed, clean, provides indoor restrooms as locked storage for backpacks.  Thanks, Jeff, we would take this tour again!

review_text:
Grand Denali Tour with Glacier Landing---

I have traveled up through Talkeetna on to Denali National Park numerous times over the last 10 years.   I had never, up until this trip, taken advantage of the Talkeetna Air Taxi service; and all I can say about that is "Shame on me!".   
First, know that I have tried to take the flight out of Denali in the past.   While I was not successful because of the weather, this trip I was advised that while the company out of the park is a great company, the flight into would potentially be better.  The flight out saved 6 hours of bus time, and weather permitting saw some cool sights, but the flight in, with glacier landing would amaze.   They were 100% right.   Second, know that I was thinking of saving some money and not doing the glacier landing.  I called Talkeetna Air and spoke with one of their employees.  That employee did not pressure sell me at all.  She explained what people like about the flight options, those with and without glacier landings, she gave me an honest account of the time in the air (15 minutes into the park, the a lot of time flying around the summit, then a landing if chosen, than a nice flight out) for a total time much longer than the flight out of the park (mind you).  She also explained what she thinks of landing on the glacier.  Explaining to me that while I have been to Alaska and hiked and seen glaciers, being on one in the Denali range in the mountains would amaze me with the vast openness and quite.  Again, she didn't try to sell me, she simply tried to explain pros and cons.  In the end, there weren't many cons other than a bit more money---and let's be honest, if you are forking out the money for the flight, you might as well not be cheap like I was going to be.  We settled on the flight and landing and it was worth EVERY PENNY!  I kid you not.  Everything about the flight was amazing.  Our pilot-- She was amazing.  There was a time when she said--ok, we are going to fly into the face of the mountain now to give you an idea of how big it is--but don't worry, we are at least a mile from the face.  It seemed like we were right next to it!!   She warned us when it might get a bit bumpy, and why, and then we were prepared and could still experience the sights that the bumpy air allowed us to see.  And the glacier landing was amazing.   To land in snow in a mountain and take off in snow on a mountain is a modern feat.  These planes they use are amazing.  And the pilots the best!  So there is that all by itself.  But to step  out and see it and listen and just exist was the best.  Every person on that flight was blown away.  Every person on that flight had a smile from ear to ear.   I am not going to lie to you--- we had perfect weather on August 21st---some of the best they had seen in a couple of weeks.  We saw Denali in all her beauty.  In fact, we saw her driving in to Talkeetna, on the flight and the next day on the bus tour (which I have done 4 times and it never gets old).  So we were blessed!  But Talkeetna air does not shy away from being honest with you about the weather.  They will not go up in the weather is bad.  And if the clouds are in but weather ok to fly, they will be open about that tour.  And they go out of their way to rebook you if necessary.  In fact, later that week while in Seward on a whale/glacier tour with Alaska Saltwater Lodge & Tours (who I highly recommend as well) we met a mother and daughter that tried to fly the day before us.  They could not because of weather.  And Talkeetna worked with them and their very busy trip (already planned) to accommodate another flight.    With that, what I recommend is you book your travel days (if going by car mind you) to Denali park a couple of days apart.  Plan the flight on the way up there.  If it doesn't work out, try to plan a reschedule for your day out of the area if going back towards Anchorage.   

Bottom line-- I will absolutely do this experience again.  I will absolutely use Talkeenta Air Taxi.   I will absolutely do the flight and glacier landing.   And I will absolutely love it.   

Oh, and one other thing.  I had my mom and dad with me.  Both in the mid 70s.  Mom a bit leery of small planes and nervous.   She did fine.  In fact, she did better than fine.  She was not once scared nor flight sick nor anything but amazed.  It was one of the highlights of her trip and it set the stage for more adventures.   

Thank you Talkeetna Air!

This may very well be the most beautiful place I have ever visited. We were in Oahu for one week and then Kauai.  Why did we not just go to Kauai for two weeks?
We had a small condo in Kapaa in the Coconut Beach area and that is where we will stay when we come again. I like the area and it is pretty easy to get everywhere from there.  There is a park nearby called Lydgate Park that would be great to take kids to or anyone leery of ocean swimming as it has 2 areas blocked off by big boulders so that there is no worry about getting in too deep or being knocked down by waves. It also has a huge playground.
We initially were holding a very expensive rental car but I kept checking and got it down to a reasonable amount. There is no charge to park anywhere we went.
Be prepared for bad roads if you go the scenic route.  Many of the scenic roads are rutted and have potholes the size of a VW bug.  When it rains on Kauai (it rains a lot), there are red mud puddles in areas that you will go to sightsee.  If you plan to hike, take it seriously.  Many of the hikes are considered to be for those more experienced hikers and you will need real hiking shoes. Also plan on slippery areas on the hike so a fall in the mud is possible. 
The rest of the island has good roads and no mud so you don’t have to engage with the mud if you don’t want to.

I was on the island of Oahu, Hawaii when my plans to visit Pearl Harbor fell through.  I didn’t want to waste one day of our two week vacation and so I decided to research how I could visit Kauai for one day. You may think that is a ridiculous idea however, once I found Air Ventures Hawaii and spoke to a representative early Wednesday morning to secure the proper flight times for Thursday I decided to book a flight to Lihue via Southwest.  We arrived at noon and our Air Ventures flight was booked for 1:30pm.  The cost was $337.08 (two passengers) for one hour.  This flight was definitely longer, less expensive, and more beautiful than our helicopter tour that we took a few days prior to this adventure.  Trisha and her assistant greeted us with a warm Aloha and they were extremely professional and helpful.  I am happy that they informed us about paying $30.00 to capture the GoPro footage of our one hour flight.  The footage from the NaPali Coast was unbelievable yet stunning!   It is well worth the money.  
Prior to boarding we were weighed and seated in a nice open air waiting room.  I would suggest that a few hours prior to the flight that you take Dramamine to ensure you will not experience any motion sickness.  I always practiced this so I didn’t have any problems on the flight.  I believe only one passenger was somewhat ill.  I think this is important because the flight is absolutely breathtaking and you simply don’t want to be ill while enjoying such an unimaginable view.  Please be mindful that Air Ventures Hawaii has no control over Mother Nature and sometimes a few bumps might occur throughout the flight.  
Nate was our pilot.  I must admit that this guy was stellar!!!  First, he has the best personality.  He welcomed us aboard as guests, explained all safety precautions, told us exactly what would happen while in flight, and even explained what we would see while on the trip.  In addition, he was a skilled aviator that paid attention to the details of safety and also provided valuable information at the same time.  I am very happy that Air Ventures Hawaii takes passenger safety seriously.  
In addition to being a good aviator the pilot did an excellent job of explaining all the different sights that we saw during the flight.  I must admit that I love seeing the Grand Canyon of the Pacific and the waterfalls however, the NaPali Coast is a sight to behold.  Nate indicated that the NaPali Coast is considered one of the most beautiful coastlines in the world.  I agree with him unequivocally!! My eyes have not seen such natural uninhabited beauty like that since visiting Bora Bora in 2007.  The beauty of the NaPali Coast is the best reason to take this flight.  In addition, if you can only spend a day on the island it will take two hours to reach the NaPali Coast and I believe much of it cannot be reached by foot.  I believe seeing the coastline from the air is unexplainable in words and unimaginable even when you see it.  Bucket list for sure!!!!!
Our day trip to Kauai was stellar because my son and I had an opportunity to see all of the natural beauty of Kauai from the sky.  If you are in search of seeing unexplainable and breathtaking beauty I would suggest Air Ventures Hawaii.  Nate was an exceptional pilot and I feel I received everything that I paid for and more.  Thanks Nate for being a wonderful host and helping my son and I make beautiful memories.  We will forever remember the time we spent over the NaPali Coast because of you!  Mahalo for everything!!!! My husband and I visited Alaska for my first time in early August.  We knew we wanted to experience a fly over Denali National Park.  After researching the various tour operators offering this service, it was a no brainer to book with Talkeetna Air Taxi.  Not only were their Trip Advisor and Google reviews great, but what sold me was their policy to rebook or refund their tours.  The other companies had a much more rigid refund policy.  For those who have never traveled to Alaska, the weather changes daily and can be dramatic as well.  

We originally booked the Mountain Explorer with a Glacier landing for the first tour time of the day.  There are multiple tour times offered throughout the day, so if the visibility or weather cancels an earlier tour, it’s possible to book a later tour if there is availability.  We left the rest of the day open in our planning just in case.  

Unfortunately, the weather was not great on the day of our tour so they called us to tell us it was cancelled.  The rest of the tour times were cancelled as well.  But they offered to rebook us on the Mountain Explorer tour the next day without the glacier landing with a refund of the difference in pricing, so we rebooked it.

When we arrived for the 4pm tour time the next day, they actually booked us on the South Side Explorer with glacier landing and we still received a refund on the difference in price.  We were happy because we did want to have a glacier landing and we didn’t even ask, it was automatically done!  

Our pilot was Luke.  He was fantastic!  Super chill and greeted us wearing jeans and a t-shirt.  I actually sat in the first passenger seat behind the cockpit and watched him fly the plane.  It was fascinating.  Each seat of the plane had a headset with volume knobs on each ear.   Luke pointed out the names of the mountain formations as we soared around them.  It was magical!  Ruth glacier is huge and glorious in the air.  Unfortunately, Denali was hiding in the clouds but the views of the other mountains was spectacular.

The glacier landing was smooth.  We had plenty of time to walk on the glacier and take pictures.  It was worth every penny to have had the opportunity to do so.

Since we sat in the same seats on our return, Luke made sure to fly back the opposite direction so we could see the views we missed on the way up.  As we left the Denali mountain range, we could see views of the Talkeetna valley and various rivers which were breathtaking!  Smooth landing back at the airport.

Talkeetna Air Taxi is the best company for a fly over to Denali Park, hands down!

review_text:
So we booked this through the Xanterra site that you get when you go to the Grand Canyon National Park site and look for activities. Right now it says that it's not available: what happened to us is that it was unavailable until spring, when they settle on the price etc. for the new tourist season. I asked to be put on an email notification so that it wouldn't sell out on the two days we had available in September, and that worked out. I was pretty persistent about checking on it with Xanterra. 
First of all, it's a really, really long day. Just be prepared for that. You get up super early to drive over and check in, then wait at the airport for the sun to rise. The plane ride over the canyon was amazing: views that were so beautiful they made me cry. I appreciated that we both got window seats with an empty middle seat between us. There are headphones with recorded narration. 
After flying over the canyon and Horseshoe Bend, you land at Lake Powell airport. We took pictures with the plane, had a bathroom break in the small airport, then met up with our Navajo nation guide for the trip to Antelope Canyon. She was very kind, patient,  and welcoming. The ride is in an open air truck  with two rows of bench seats. There is an overhead cover and there are seat belts. She took us into the area and then up to the canyon. I was a little worried because multiple buses pulled up and lots of people got out, but the guides handled it beautifully. Each group waited while the one ahead went into each area, took photos while listening to the guide, and then moved ahead. Very well organized. I had never been in a slot canyon and it was truly beautiful and very cool. The photos were amazing; our guide was full of tips about phone settings and positions in the canyon for various types of pictures. 
We were taken to a water sports/activities center where we could refill water bottles and use the restroom while we waited outside. It was a little awkward. There we met up with another group and went through metal detectors before boarding a bus to the Lake Powell dam. At the foot of the dam we got into small open boats and floated down the Colorado river and around Horseshoe Bend, stopping to look at rock formations, wild horses (!),  and views along the way. We got out of the boats once at a spot that had porta potties and amazingly clear Native American hieroglyphics. The water was too cold for swimming unless you were very hardy. The float trip was lovely, but a bit long since you couldn't move around very much on the boat and it was very sunny/hot. Also, the lunch provided was okay but not much....and they gave it to us while we were waiting for the bus and told us not to eat it on the bus, so we started eating before the bus and had to stop...it was strangely inefficient and not enough food for the day. Bring snacks and refill your water whenever you get the chance. 
Bus ride home was worst part; comfortable but long with only one stop. Those of us who had done the plane part of the trip had to wait as the bus wound its way through Grand Canyon Village and slowly disembarked the others, so very late getting back to our vehicle and a really long time between bathroom breaks! All in all, a long day but so many great experiences!

review_text: We just completed our first Grand Canyon visit and the Scenic River Canyon Tour was the absolute best part of the trip. The entire tour could not have ran smoother. We arrived at the airport at 5:45 am, about 15 minutes from the El Tovar Lodge at Grand Canyon Village. Easy check in. We were provided a light breakfast with muffins, fruit, juice and coffee. We gathered in a comfortable lounge while waiting for the departure. We boarded about 6:20 with departure at 6:30. There were 6 passengers on our plane, every seat a window seat. Our pilot was delightful and informative. Although the plane was small, the flight was super smooth and thrilling. No matter how long you look, you can not see the depth and detail of the canyon from the rim like you can from the air. It is something I will never forget. After about a 50 minute flight, we landed in Page. We were soon met at the airport by a Navajo guide that would take us via 4-wheel vehicle to Antelope Canyon, a 20 min drive. The truck was open-air, so a little cool, but not too bad. At the canyon, the guide took us through, stopping and explaining exactly what we were seeing and the science and history around it. She gave us all tips on how to photograph the canyon and made this part of the tour a highlight. I promise you it will be the most beautiful place that you never heard of. After completing this part of the tour, we boarded a bus for a 10-12 min ride, and were provided a boxed lunch. The next stop was the canyon river portion of the tour. There we boarded a raft with our river guide 'Jenny'. You can sit in the provided cushion seating or the large pontoons. I recommend sitting in the seats just forward of Jenny's console. Those seats have back rests. Most folks ate their lunch as we headed down the river. Iced water and lemonade was provided. The 3 hour ride was incredible! It was slow and smooth, just fast enough to create a gentle, and appreciated breeze. You find yourself looking in all directions. The vistas in front and behind you. And the massive walls of rock on each side. In many places the 46 degree water was crystal clear and fish are easily seen. Jenny was a compete joy. She was funny, informative, courteous and helpful. She constantly informed us as to what we were seeing, and added great stories along the way. We made a stop along the way on a small sandy beach. Bath rooms are provided. You're also able to check out some  petroglyphs on the  canyon walls. After about a 30 min break, we re-boarded and continued down the river. More incredible views were along the way to Lees Ferry, where our motor coach back to the airport was waiting. There are bathrooms here as well. The bus was very comfortable and most folks napped on the way back. We stopped at Cameron Trading Post for about 30 min to stretch our legs and purchase souvenirs if you're inclined. The bus driver also was courteous and informative as we drove past more vistas along Desert View Drive. We returned to where we started,12 hours earlier. I can't think of any better way to experience the canyon. From the air, the Colorado River at the base and the rim during the drive back. I highly recommend the tour. It's a little pricey but you won't regret it.

The Scenic Airlines Grand Canyon Connoisseur Tour is a great way to see the south rim of the Grand Canyon if you are visiting from Las Vegas. One hour of flying there, then transfer by bus to tour the canyon for 3 hours, and then a one hour ride back.  They will also pick you up and drop you off from your Las Vegas hotel.  

However you decide to see the canyon, scour the internet for the best price and tour to suit your needs.  There’s a ton of choices and different prices for the same types of tours, so shop around.

Scenic, Papillion and Grand Canyon Airlines are all the same company, departing from the Boulder City airport, located about 45 minutes from the strip.  We found the best price for the tour with Scenic.  Grand Canyon Airlines has the exact same tour, but was slightly more.  There was also a difference in price, depending on what time of day you book your tour.  Our 9:15AM tour was the most expensive, the 12:30PM was less, and the 6:15AM was the least expensive.

They weigh you before you get on the plane, and that includes your purse, camera, water bottle, etc., so keep that in mind.  If you get motion sickness, take dramamine or bonine beforehand.  The plane is small (about 19 passengers), and it got quite bumpy for a good portion of the flight.  Do not pay extra for a window seat.  Our plane had two seats on each side and the windows are very large.  If you are a couple they generally seat you together, so one of you should get a window seat.

Now the GOOD:  
Beautiful aerial view of the Hoover Dam, Lake Mead, the Colorado River and the Grand Canyon.
Bus tour took you to Bright Angel and Mather Point. This is the most impressive and the widest and deepest part of the canyon.  Plenty of time to souvenir shop too.
Gigi, our bus driver was fabulous!  She was a lot of fun and gave a  lot of interesting information.  They also had another guide to speak Japanese for part of our group.

review_text:
This was the activity that I chose for mine and my husband's recent trip to Arizona - the 12 1/2 hour Scenic Canyon River Adventure that covered air, land and water. And if I don't say so myself, I chose well. 

Our excursion began at 6 am at the Grand Canyon Airport - less than a mile from The Grand Hotel where we were staying. At check-in we were weighed (this included anything we were carrying) and given a boxed breakfast (OJ, small yogurt, banana muffins, cheese stick and a granola bar). Color-coded wrist bands (green for our group) were affixed to our arm. At promptly 6:30 am approxiately 20 persons boarded the small aircraft with each one having their own window seat (we didn't have to pay extra for it). Take off was smooth (and uneventful) and after ten minutes or so the Canyon appeared in all of its splendor as the sun rose casting a myriad of colors - soft pinks, deep reds and warm golds wherever its rays touched ... simply breathtaking! There were headphones on the plane that provided info on the scenes unfolding below as the plane soared onward. A half hour into our flight the clear blue waters of Lake Powell emerged. All too soon we touched down (smoothly) on the other side of the Canyon in Page, AZ. 

After a fifteen minute wait at the small airport, our group was shuttled onto retro-fitted pick-up trucks for an often bumpy ride to Antelope Canyon where other tour groups were already gathered. I tend to be a bit claustrophobic so thankfully it wasn't very dark inside the narrow passageways. Light spilled from above creating some spectacular photo-op's. Upon reaching the end of the long tunnel we then turned around and retraced our steps back to where we started. Loaded back onto the pick-up's, we were then driven to the Colorado River Discovery building in Page, AZ.

It was another 30 or 45 minutes before several large coach buses pulled in front of the building. Dozens of people were assembled and wore a variety of colored coded wrist-bands. Each person was handed a boxed lunch (turkey sandwich, chips, chocolate chip cookies and an apple) as they boarded the buses. We were driven through a dark, 2-mile inclined tunnel that brought us down to the river basin at Glen Canyon Dam. Given hard-hats to wear as we were told it was mandatory due to its being a government run facility, we walked a short distance over to the large rafts. Each raft easily accommodated 18 - 20 people. My husband and I were fortunate to have been on the vessel led by Brett, an informative and often amusing guide who regaled us with many stories and folklore of the Colorado River. He also played a mean recorder! For fifteen miles we floated ever so slowly down the majestic river surrounded by massive stone walls that stretched upwards hundreds of feet. Twice Brett made two short stops where a few brave (or crazy) souls jumped into frigid 47 degree water and we trekked a short distance to spot ancient petroglyphs drawn on rock walls. Upon docking we were resorted according to wrist band colors and directed to the appropriate coach bus. Most, including myself, fell asleep during the two hour return trip back to the Grand Canyon Airport. 

To say that the entire excursion - plane, land and float was spectacular and incredibly humbling is an understatement. I highly recommend it! If you have the opportunity to take this tour, DO IT! It was money well spent for the experience of a life-time!

TIP: Wear a hat and bring and use plenty of sunscreen. The tour company provides water.

Anyway, on the day, our pick-up was running 10 or 15 minutes late (no big deal) and after collecting four other couples, the drive to Boulder City airstrip took around 40 minutes. Outside on the apron were numerous helicopters and around the corner sat the airplanes. Lots of people were arriving from different places for a number of early flights. Unfortunately for us, only 4 of the 8 passengers booked on our plane had managed to drag themselves out of bed for the pick-up, and our flight was cancelled. So to the flight. The plane was small and cosy with large viewing windows. The crew were very friendly and accommodating. We had headsets that alternated between playing an audio travel guide with useful information on the area, and a cheesy soundtrack that I reckon was taken from "Blazing saddles" !  The flight was nice and smooth (taking into account the odd airpocket that wouldn't constitute turbulence, but which still caused my other half to attempt to surgically remove my left bicep, using only her fingernails and her teeth ! !) Would we recommend Grand Canyon Airlines? Definitely.

review_text:
After my cruise ship floatplane excursion, a long-awaited journey for a special birthday treat, was cancelled due 'high winds', something that wasn't apparent that warm and sunny afternoon, especially as the floatplanes kept taking off and landing right next to the ships, including the company that was doing my cancelled excursion, I then quickly shopped around onshore for a replacement flight with limited shore-time left.

Two attempted bookings failed - someone scored a last seat just before me, and another company couldn't find enough passengers to make it worthwhile. Thankfully the remaining one, SeaWind Aviation, had room for me on my preferred aircraft - an original radial engined DHC-2 Beaver. As a retired airline pilot, it was Beavers flying overhead as a small kid that helped seed my interest in aviation.

Not only was SeaWind less expensive than the cancelled cruise ship excursion, but I got picked up from the ship by co-owner Lesley, driven a very short distance to their terminal and dock facilities, and soon after was sitting up the front right behind that rumbling radial engine - marvellous!

The pilot, Mike, not only handled the Beaver on water and in the air like a maestro but removed all the bumps that had been responsible for the previous flight's 'cancellation'. I suspect overbooking was the real reason for that, but I was so fortunate to fall into the friendly care of Lesley and Mike from SeaWind, and that marvellous old, shiny and obviously well-maintained Beaver.

The flight not only took in the advertised sightseeing around Ketchikan harbour, but went well off along valleys, between forested mountains and across several islands to make ripples on a perfectly smooth isolated island lake, landing and taking off just for fun :) 

Headsets and an intercom allowed Mike to answer passengers' questions along the way. We returned to Ketchikan, landing right beside the cruise ships and tying up at the dock about 150m from my ship - an easy walk back, sporting a new 'Beaver' cap, rather than trouble Lesley for another ride :)

I'm still grinning at the memory of that ride and so proud of my 'birthday' hat :)

review_text:
I booked a trip to Traitor's Cove directly from the website, which was pretty easy to navigate, and received confirmation of the booking within 24 hours (it might have been closer to 10 hours). 

The directions in terms of where to meet were very clear (by the berth next to our cruise ship's), and the vans were clearly marked and easy to find. It was a short drive to the Seawind office/dock.

We flew in one of the 7 passenger De Havillands. It was surprisingly comfortable. We spent a few minutes figuring out seating, which did worry me. (What if someone lied about their weight and they balanced the plane incorrectly?) However, the flight went very smoothly and we were able to see a lot of the Tongass National Forest on our way to Traitor's Cove. On the way back, one of the kids decided he wanted my seat (to be closer to his little brother), and so we switched with no discernible difference as to the smoothness of the flight. I guess the weight balancing didn't need to be that precise!

Our plane had two-way headsets which the kids tested out. The flight itself was somewhere between 20-30 minutes long. Our pilot provided commentary on the way out, but gave us time to just look out and relax on the way back.

After the flight, we took a short drive, and then a short walk to the viewing platform. Along the way, our guide reiterated the bear viewing/safety guidelines, and pointed out native plants and fresh bear scat.

We were the first group of the day to arrive at the viewing platform, where the USFS ranger pointed out a bear who was already fishing for salmon. In all, we saw 7 bears (or maybe 8?), including one who walked right under our platform, and a mama bear fishing with her two cubs. We also saw salmon jumping, and two bald eagles. We stayed for about 2 hours - one group arrived and left while we were there, and another arrived about 30 minutes before we left. During that time, the platform was never crowded, and there was plenty of space for everyone to get a good view. My binoculars were handy at times, but not necessary, as most of the bears were very close.

This was an incredible experience! That being said, I understand that it is heavily dependent on Mother Nature's cooperation and I was lucky. We were told all flights the previous day had been cancelled due to the weather, and that viewing in July had been poor as the lack of rain had affected the salmon run. However, the easy communication, the smooth and scenic flight, and the friendly and knowledgeable guides made all the parts under human control excellent (and the bears were great as well :-)

Bruce (he’s also Dr. Bruce, a retired research scientist!) and Val were very professional and took good care of us. We were unsure of this morning’s trip as the weather forecast was not looking good. Rain and clouds were about to roll in when we got to the airport. Val greeted us cheerfully, checked us in and went through the safety briefing with us thoroughly. I immediately knew that they took safety seriously. We then waited as we were early for our scheduled departure. It started to rain shortly thereafter and Bruce then called us into the office and showed us the big rain clouds over the Lihue & Hanalei area on the computer. He was very honest and told us that we will likely not have clear views over some areas. So he gave us a choice to reschedule, a refund or to go ahead with the tour (assuring us it was safe to do so). What an honest and professional business! We decided to go ahead and was prepared for a less than stellar experience. Boy, were we wrong! While it was cloudy, the sights were still wonderful as Bruce expertly navigated through the clouds and showed us the spectacular Na Pali Coast and the breathtaking Waimea Canyon. We had to turn around at Hanalei due to the storm clouds (again safety first!) while some other operators decided to go through the area. I knew this as I could hear all the chatter over the radio. A couple others did turn around and followed Bruce’s lead. He must be well respected by the flying community! We made it back to Lihue airport safely with full of wonderful memories. Thank you Bruce for your wonderful sense of humor and knowledge about the island. I enjoyed being your “co-pilot”!

review_text: We (2 of us) enjoyed a flight with Captain Doug mid-July while visiting Kauai for vacation and celebrating my birthday.  I discovered Wings Over Kauai reading Trip Advisor reviews.  We have been on several helicopters tours- over Oahu, Maui, and the big island as well as a tour in the Caribbean over Antigua. Flying with Wings Over Kauai, we had the advantage of not having to ride with other parties, he enjoyed sitting up front with Captain Doug, and I enjoyed having the back seat to myself to see and take pictures from both sides.  We were initially hesitant about reviews noting how fly higher than helicopter tours, but we didn’t think there was much difference and it didn’t at all effecting the view or taking pictures.  I think we actually captured better pictures.  We went on a boat tour along NaPali coast line the day prior and would agree with previous reviews that it’s so worth seeing the NaPali coastline by boat and by air.  Even after visiting the canyon, the views are so different flying over the canyon.  I experience motion sickness so I didn’t know if this experience would be different.  I took medication prior flying, ate the ginger chews offered, and thought I did better on this flight than helicopter tours.  The windows are closed so don’t have the breeze coming in the window like the helicopter but there was enough air and coolness that motion sickness wasn’t triggered.  I later too found the ginger chews are sold at the ABC stores.  We have learned from previous tours to wear dark colored clothes so there is no reflection in the windows when taking pictures.  Gina was efficient in checking us in and coordinating preparation for our flight.  We appreciated how in addition to the pictures we captured, Gina took our picture in front of the Cessna before departing, shared the pictures by e-mail, as well as gave us a CD of music during our flight afterward with our picture on the front cover.  During our flight time, a Hawaiian Airlines plane landed and there were many helicopters flying the same route around the island.  Captain Doug did a great job toggling back and forth communicating with the tower while letting us know where and what we were flying over.  He took extra time flying at different angles/circling around waterfalls and points of interest we pointed out.  Many reviews highlight a cost savings booking with Wings Over Kauai. We have no regrets not booking a helicopter tour and are so glad we stumbled upon learning about Wings Over Kauai through Trip Advisor.

review_text:
We really had a great time with Wings Over Kauai.  We were in the area for a day and a half on the Pride Of America cruise ship.  I decided to schedule our flight for 930am the second day.  The first day we arrived it was pretty cloudy and rainy, so I was bummed that the weather was going to stay the same and we wouldn't see much.  Thankfully the second day it was totally clear and nice!  Even the top of Waialeale was clear!

The day of our trip we were picked up promptly near the cruise ship as arraigned.  We went over the basics- safety, weigh-in, and some pictures next to the plane.  Our pilot was Josh (a former American Airlines pilot), and he got us buckled in to our assigned seats.  I was in the copilot seat, and my wife was behind me.  Once in the air, Josh told us lots of facts about what we were seeing while music played.  The Na Pali coast was beautiful and we had great viewing weather.  I did get a bit of haze in my pictures, which looked worse on the camera's LCD than the final picture (I used a telephoto lens with a polarizing filter).  Before we knew it, it was time to land.  I really enjoyed getting to listen to air traffic control the whole time also.

Once back at the airport, they gave everyone a free gift (I won't ruin the surprise).  They also offered to sell us a DVD of the full flight, filmed by GoPros mounted under the wings and inside the cabin.  The price was very reasonable, and it arrived by the time we got home.  It was a great keepsake to have, and the views were so much better than what I captured on my camera.  They offered to drop us off back at the cruise ship or the mall, and gave my wife a flower for her hair.  Everyone we met was extremely nice and we really enjoyed the flight.

One note, if you have even the slightest problem with motion sickness, take a dramamine pill before you fly.  We were lucky to have a pretty smooth flight, but small slow planes like this are more prone to thermals and winds than large jets.  We experienced a few quick stomach-drops, that felt kind of a like a roller coaster hill.  My wife did feel a little airsick, but the dramamine stopped her from throwing up.  They do have a cooler on board with sprite and ginger chews, but better safe than sorry.

Don't hesitate to get a great view of Kauai, book a flight!

My only regret is that my English is not good enough to match my feelings towards those wonderful people on the ground and in the air. Thank you Ellen and Josh.

There's a reason Wings Over Kauai Air Tours is the # 1 rated activity for Kauai. My wife and I recently returned from our 2nd visit to Kauai. Having been stationed on Oahu and trained on the Big Island, I can say Kauai is the most beautiful Hawaiian Island. Wings Over Kauai is the BEST method to see the landscape. During our most recent visit, we took my wife's parents and her older brother. The hour long air tour was the highlight of our group's excursions. 

We booked the one hour Air Van Private Charter, and Josh was our pilot / guide while airborne. Dori, Ellen and Millie (the owner's dog) greeted us at the hangar that is shared with several smaller air tour operators. The easiest route to their hangar is drive towards LIH (Lihue airport), pass the curbside pick up and drop off and you'll see the fixed wing hangar less than a mile on the right side. Keep LIH runways on your right side, and you'll see the Wings Over Kauai signage. Check-in consists of weigh-ins for aircraft balance, a model of Kauai to point out routes (each dependent on weather), and addressing any concerns passengers have pre-flight. Once check-in was complete, we had ample time to use restrooms on site and view aircraft departing and arriving into LIH.

Prior to boarding the aircraft, a group photo was taken plane side. GoPro cameras are mounted to each wing and at least one interior camera faces passengers. My wife was given a Kukui nut necklace for the photos and as a gift. Once on board, BOSE two-way headphones are given to each passenger for communication with your pilot and each other. For airplane enthusiasts such as myself, you'll enjoy hearing ATC and other aircraft in the area during the flight. I really liked this feature as you'll quickly notice all the aircraft circling Kauai are constantly in radio contact and sharing information regarding weather or terrain features. A cooler with refreshments and snacks is also provided in the cabin, a nice touch. Highlights of our flight included two whale pods sighted on windward side of the island, breathtaking views inside Waimea Canyon and the beach views from 5,000 feet. We even passed over our condo in Princeville and took photographs to share with future renters, review forthcoming. 

Total airtime was over 60 minutes, and the blend of Josh's commentary and background music was perfect. Everyone on board had questions for Josh, and he did a great job explaining the island's legends, culture and environment. As we taxied back to the hangar, a DVD or BluRay copy of your flight is offered. The 3 GoPro cameras capture everything you saw during the flight, and interior commentary is optional. Dori gave us a CD with their promotional video and the cover included one of our group's pre-flight photos. Ten minutes after we landed, my smartphone showed an e-mail from Wings Over Kauai with five group photographs Dori took. Customer service is above and beyond at Wings Over Kauai.

Why Wings Over Kauai Air Tours vs. helicopters or other guides? The seating is spacious, and you have more flexibility in where you can place passengers. All passengers have a port and starboard window. Driving into Waimea Canyon doesn't guarantee a view, we've made that drive before. My mother-in-law opted out of the flight just prior to departure. The ground crew never made her feel guilty and were supportive of her decision. You cover more airspace vs. the helicopter tours, and you literally fly above them. The tour is priced extremely well, and environmental impact is low. Don't hesitate to call or e-mail Wings Over Kauai for assistance in planning. This is the must do activity for Kauai! review_text:

Since I have a group of 6 with varying budgets, I Tripadvisored and found Wings Over Kauai. For the whole 6-seater plane and an hour long tour, it costed us a little more than $500 after taxes in TOTAL. And it was basically a private tour.

The flying route will take you to all of the main attractions on the island of Kauai. Na Pali Coast, the Waimea Canyon and all the wonderful waterfalls, etc. We were very lucky with the weather, so the oldest of Hawaiian Islands, Kauai was completely revealed to us. After seeing most of the main islands, I have to say it is the most beautiful in my eyes. 

But, really it is the people of Wings Over Kauai that truly made this tour so special. Started from the booking, planning, pick-up and finally the tour itself, everyone involved was courteous and very helpful. Ellen handled most of the pre-flight arrangement, she knows about our ship better than I did. As it was to leave earlier than I thought I would on the day of the trip. And most of all, Josh our pilot, was really knowledgable and have this genuine friendliness about him that just made all of us enjoyed our trip so much more. The fact he speaks some Chinese and good looking just made my mom and all of her friends felt very much "at ease" (they were really worried about the size of the plane when I told them about the tour). They ended up spending all of the preflight time chatting and teasing Josh and totally forgot about their initial worries (it went so bad as one of them was asking if he'd like to be set up for a date with her daughter. at which point I had to intervene :). Since he use to be a commercial pilot for the American Airline, he handled our 6-seaters with ease and professional smoothness. Even my partner who usually gets really nauseated with a small plane, barely had any problems this time. And the landing was very smooth, I clapped. As a tour guide, Josh was equally up to the task. One thing I really loved, he had different the background music ready when flying over different locations. 

All in all I thoroughly enjoyed the tour, it was hands down the least expensive and the most exciting tour we did on the whole Hawaiian tour.  

Couple of tips: 
1)Book ahead, if possible with a group of 5-6 or 2 for the whole plane (they also have a two-seater). Otherwise, it's $125 per person as of Nov. 2013.
2)For pickup, ask for the Pier if possible. Although their pickup spot isn't too far from the Pier, it's about 5-10 mins walk and has a convenient store there that sells much cheaper items than the ship store.
3)The only downside with the plane tour is, maybe with a helicopter you can get closer to the scenic location. However at triple the price, I wonder it would be worth it any more.

review_text:
After reviewing a number of air charters, we chose Wings Over Kauai based primarily on the Number 1 rating here at TA, plus the excellent reviews from previous customers. It is also cheaper - by half, at least - than a helicopter tour (for the same 60-75 minute tour), and if you are eco-minded, apparently the fixed-wing aircraft of Wings uses much less fuel than a copter. Though it seems that all the companies offering air tours have terrific safety records, it is also my belief that fixed-wing aircraft are generally safer than helicopters. We are joining with all those who have given Wings an excellent rating with no hesitation, and provide our recommendation with great enthusiasm! 
From the moment we arrived at the airport, we were made to feel welcome and at ease, should we have had any anxiety. We conversed with the receptionist, who was the owner's daughter, and she was terrific. She handled the few administrative details with efficiency and again, made us feel extremely comfortable. She also took our photo before we boarded the plane, which was much appreciated.
Our flight had another couple, and all four of us had window seats (all the seats are window seats, but based on the flight of the aircraft, it appears that you may have better views of things by being seated on the right side of the airplane, as we all were able/instructed to do). Water and soda was available if you wanted it, as well as some remedies for motion sickness, if the need arose (my wife actually felt a little queasy during a portion of the flight and took one of the lozenges provided, which made her feel fine almost immediately).
I have flown in helicopters several times (all for work) and never in a small plane, so I was anxious to compare the distinctions between the experiences. I was immediately struck by the smoothness and quality of the flight, even in some mild turbulence. Our pilot was extremely knowledgeable and friendly, and something about his manner in the airplane exuded confidence (which is important in a pilot!). 
The views from the airplane were simply amazing. The mountains, beaches, canyons, waterfalls, and caves were astounding in their beauty and ruggedness. The view of developed properties (e.g., golf courses, plantations, hotels/resorts) was also outstanding. The flight path covered nearly the whole island (I am not sure why about 1/4 [-less? Generally, from east of Princeville to Lihue] of the island is not on the tour) and flew over all the spots you would care to see. Be prepared to take many, many photos, of course (One slight negative regarding this concerns the fact that you are taking your pictures out of a window - the views you get through the window are amazing, but some photos are subject to get a little glare - not the fault of Wings; just be aware of this).
Once we landed, we were given a copy of a DVD which highlighted the views we experienced during the flight (these are "stock" clips, but still provide a nice memento of the trip - the cover of the DVD is one of the photos taken of you before you board the plane). Later that evening, the owners contacted us via email to thank us and encourage our review on TA (a nice touch!).
We met another couple at a luau a couple days later who had flown with Wings a day after we did. They flew when there was much more rain in the mountains, so they shared how the pilot stated they were seeing more waterfalls than were present in the days beforehand. I mention this to say that I don't think weather will likely stop your flight (this is up to Wings, but I think it likely that you will encounter rain at some point during the flight - this was no problem and didn't really diminish the quality of photos that we took).
It seems that all the travel folks recommend seeing Kauai by air during your visit. I think this is a valid recommendation, and I can say with no reluctance that you will not be disappointed by booking with Wings Over Kauai.

While in the plane, you wear headphones with a mic attached, through which you can hear the pilot's running commentary about what you're seeing. You can also ask questions and make comments that everyone in the plane can hear.

Have your long camera lenses ready for the stunning views as you see miles of coastline, blue waters, waterfalls, coffee groves, fancy resorts, celebrity houses, an Indian temple, the cruise port, the Na Pali coast, Waimea Canyon and possibly even whales.

It's a thrilling approximately 60 minute ride that will leave you on a high for a few days and provide you with some fabulous photo memories.

You are given a complimentary previously filmed short DVD as a keepsake of the trip and they e-mail you a digital photo of yourself next to the plane. 

For $125 per person, it beat the price of the much more expensive helicopter rides and yet still provided one of the absolute highlights of our vacation. We recommend it! 

NOTE: Complimentary parking available in front of the check-in terminal. 
It's recommended you book the flight early in your vacation in case it has to be postponed due to weather conditions. We were lucky to have a beautiful clear day!

The fixed wing plane was good value and Bruce was a fount of information.  The fixed winged plane does not go into the canyons but looking at helicopters that did, I was glad that the plane did not do that -  a sudden gust of wind could be extremely dangerous.
Kauai is beautiful from the air and with so many contrasts it is a delight to see.  We had seen the Waimea Canyon from the road the previous day and the plane view gave a wonderfully different perspective.  Flying over Princeville and the northern coast was also lovely and gave us an idea of whether we wanted to visit there or not.  If you are a golfer then there are some very interesting and beautiful golf courses.
Be ready with your camera and dont lean it against the window - it damages the windows.  The opportunities for photographs are quick so you really need to be prepared.  Video of the trip would be great.  Bruce's son has produced a CD with photographs taken of customers before the trip and highlights of what is seen on a typical trip.  A great souvenir.  They also present the women passengers with a Kuki nut lei.  
Bruce was an agronomist and is able to tell you all about the crops and flora of the island.  The forest of abiza trees from Africa are beautiful - hopefully they are not an invasive pest.
We were lucky enough to see some waterfalls as there had been a lot of rain recently.  The extinct volcano in the middle of the island has the highest record of rainfall in comparison with other parts of Kauai so there were quite a few waterfalls on he northern side.
Ellen provides air sickness ginger candy for those with queezy stomachs and cold drinks in the form of cola and water.  Bruce goes through all the safety checks before take off including the use of life jackets.
The plane we flew had been made in Gippsland (Australia) and took six passengers as well as the pilot.  It was comfortable.  Note that the seating of passengers take place according to weight so you may not get the seat you had hoped for.  However all seats have good views and Bruce will point out places and things of interest if you advise him before hand of your particular interests.
The fixed plane cost is roughly half the cost of a helicopter flight.  It is good value indeed.
The waiting area looks over the helicopter landing area and you can sit in the open air and watch the helicopters taking off.
