review_text:
Often one reads or hears great reviews and then can't help but be let down.  Such was not the case with Wings Over Kauai unless you count being let down gently at the end of the flight.  Before the flight, we were sent a map showing us how to walk from where our ship docked to the ABC store, and Ellen (one of the owners of the business) promptly picked us up at 9 AM in a nice van so all six of us in our group could travel to the airport together. 

Our pilot Shaun couldn’t have been kinder.  We were expecting Bruce, as we didn't realize the company had two pilots and had only read about Bruce, but Shaun was very competent and cordial and welcomed questions and also was cool about others pointing out nearby planes or helicopters, which is important for a pilot to be good about making people feel free to do.

Ellen also couldn't have been kinder.  She gave me a kakua nut necklace for booking the trip (at least one woman from another plane tour booked by our group also got a lei) and gave all the females flowers for their hair, and took our photo by the plane and had that as a cover to a DVD on the highlights of their tour, which she gave for free to each party in our party of six who didn’t live with another party member (which meant 4 DVDs for our group!).   She also supplied a ginger candy to each passenger to help with motion sickness in case anyone was susceptible to that (none in out plane were, but in one of our other two groups to go up, I think two or three were), and also gave us free waters.

The sights on this tour were amazing and made us feel like we need not bother driving to Waimea Canyon, so we scratched that from what to do after the tour and headed to Hanalei at Shaun's suggestion.  Shaun doubled back over some spots to be sure people on both sides of the plane got to view things like a blow hole.  The only drawback I saw of this tour was that the plane can’t dip into places like a helicopter can, so keep that in mind if you really want to get down into places (up close to falls and such). But also keep in mind that the Wings Over Kauai flight is far less expensive than a helicopter ride (it’s $520 with tax for a plane, so if you have only 4 people, it’s $130 with tax, but if you have six like we did, it was only $86.67/person, and the helicopter on Kauai will likely run you over $210/person) and the people simply couldn’t have been nicer, so I was pleased to do business with them.  

Maren, their office worker, is also sweet as molasses and a pleasure to correspond with both via email and phone; she was also quite cute in making a typo and writing "vowel renewal ceremony" in an email, which resulted in my husband and I starting off our 25th anniversary vow renewal ceremony with a joke about how our ceremony was not a vowel renewal, even with how almost half the Hawaiian alphabet is comprised of vowels, as it's not about I or U, but about Aaaa and Eee and sometimes "WHY?" In one picture we can count 14 waterfalls (I’ll share it so you can see for yourself).  Bruce answered every question asked of him and did a fantastic job keeping everyone engaged.  

After landing, we were promptly presented with a DVD that had our picture on the cover (taken before we took off).  It contained a video of the tour (previously filmed and produced to music).  Ellen dropped us off at the shopping center where we met her (a short walk from the ship), but offered to take us back to the ship.  We opted to grab a bottle of water at the ABC Store and walk back to the ship (with plenty of time to spare before the ship’s departure).  On the walk back to the ship, I received an e-mail from Ellen that contained the pre-flight pictures (the same ones on the DVD) and a nice “thank you” note.  Again, a very nice touch!

Bottom line, Captain Bruce, Ellen and Jeanne were great!  Their #1 Rated Tour is not hype, it is for real!  Courteous, professional, knowledgeable and safe!  Treat yourself to this tour….you won’t regret it!

I'm the same when I'm a passenger in someone else's car, so... yeah.

A few final pointers: make sure you budget for it, make sure you book in advance, make sure you take photo ID with you, bear in mind that flights may be cancelled if the weather is unfit for flying or if there are too few passengers for the flight to be viable - always call a few hours before your flight to check.

review_text:
First helicopter ride for us and we liked it.

We departed from the Grand Canyon airport, and be aware that Maverick is the second airport turn after the turnaround, not the first.

The reception area is very modern and nice.  You have to pay, show ID, get weighed (done very discreetly), and read an advisory page before meeting the pilot (who will call your name when he is ready to roll).

There were 3 other people sharing our flight.  The pilot does introductions, provides a short trip and safety briefing, and then takes you out to the machine.  They snap pictures of you with the helicopter and pilot (to sell upon return), do a few more safety briefing things, have you snap on an inflatable flotation device around your waist, and then place you inside the machine.  They use your weight to determine where you should sit and you may not sit next to your party.  We soon understood that isn't a big deal as you also must wear headphones and speak into a microphone so everyone hears everything said for the entire trip so it's not like you can be whispering to your spouse anyway.  You also get belted in via a 3 point system that is pretty robust.  You have to sort of climb in, and there is a guy to help.  It is no harder than getting into a mini-van.  The cabin is heated/cooled so you don't need a coat.  It seemed like the back row seats were a bit more spacious--but they all may be the same.  One of us sat in front, and one in back, and we thought the views were equally good.

The pilot is very good at describing both the aspects of the ride, and also the Canyon below.  The best "buzz" feeling is when the helicopter first goes over the canyon after the run over the woods--it is pretty thrilling.

The entire ride was smooth as glass and we never had a whiff of fear.  It was really both thrilling and calming.

This is a fairly expensive attraction, but we thought it was worth the money.  Upon landing there is opportunity to ask more questions and take more pictures, and they also offer to sell you their professional-taken picture just before take-off, and also a CD.  The pilot lingers to see if anyone is going to tip him and that is a bit awkward but there is zero pressure.

We were glad we went.

For our annual holiday my boyfriend and I went to Las Vegas with the intention of visiting the Grand Canyon.  We had looked at various options and we eventually decided on visiting by doing something we've never done, that is to visit by helicopter.

We had booked the tour through our hotel and had decided on the Grand Canyon West Tour - Tribal Spirit.  If you go on to their website and look for this tour you'll be able to get a more detailed breakdown of what the tour entails.

The plane ride to the Canyon was amazing and equally amazing was the helicopter ride into the Canyon itself.  It really is difficult to get a perspective of how massive the Canyon is but going in by helicopter makes you see just why it's so impressive.  We got to spend about 20 minutes in the Canyon which really is just enough time to take a few pictures.  It's worth noting that when we transferred from the plane to the helicopter we had to wait around 20 minutes for the helicopter to arrive from Las Vegas as it had left after the plane.

After the helicopter into the Canyon you can take the shuttle bus to three different areas; Guano Point, Eagle Point (where the Skywalk is) and Hualapai Indian Village.  The tour gives you only 1.5 hours to do all three of the sites.  The shuttle is a bit hit and miss.  When we went it was very busy owing to the government shut down making it a 30 minute wait for the shuttle bus so we went straight to Guano Point for some amazing views.  The tour was included a lunch voucher for the cafe that is at Guano Point but you really don't have time for it and we didn't use it.  We spent 15 minutes there before having to get on the shuttle back to the plane.  There was another couple with us who had bought the Skywalk tour with the package to save time but they were unable to use it either.  

Even with it not being busy I would say that 1.5 hours is not enough time to enjoy both Guano Point and Eagle Point with the Skywalk when you factor in the travel times.  You've paid a lot of money of money for the tour to enjoy the view and take it all in but found most of my time seeing it behind the lens of my camera just to make sure I had something to remember it by.  With the time available you have to decide on doing Guano Point or the Skywalk at Eagle Point and not both.  If you've done the helicopter ride into the Canyon itself then I wouldn't bother with the Skywalk and just go straight to Guano Point, unless you really like the idea of seeing the Canyon right under your feet.  If you are intending to do the Skywalk then purchase your ticket through Maverick Helicopters as it will save time queuing when you're there.

I did mention to the pilot on our return that there was not enough time to get lunch at Guano Point, but there was no offer of refunding or telling us to ask when we got back to the airfield for a refund.  It's a use it or loose it.  Not good enough.  I would advise taking a sandwich or something as it's a long time without food and the pick up from the hotel is 06:30am.  

All in all I felt that the company should be more realistic about the time you will actually have to enjoy the views.  The tours look like you get to do lots of things but you don't.  Prioritise what you want to do.

review_text:
Having read some of the reviews, we were not sure whether to splash out on a helicopter tour for three of us, but we're so glad we did.  We booked a 25 minute ride with Maverick, from the little airport south of Tuseyan near the Canyon's South Rim.   We got there half an hour early.  The terminal building is bright, clean and very efficient.  We checked in and were weighed (no, they don't tell you how much you weigh - you just stand on a plate and nobody is any the wiser!).  We then waited til we were called by the pilot.  Ours was called Cory and not only was he the most handsome pilot there, he was also a really great tour guide.   

We had a thorough safety briefing and were then seated according to the plan they have, which I guess is based on the weight of each passenger to better balance the aircraft.   We donned life jackets (as we fly over the Colorado River, it's a legal requirement), our safety belts, our head phones and microphones, and then we were off.   First, we flew over the ponderosa forest toward the canyon.  My husband and I hate heights but we were absolutely fine.  My son and I were in the front and the helicopter was the type that meant we could see right down to the floor all round - great visibility.  Even in the back, the seats are higher than the front to aid visibility.   We spent about five minutes getting to the canyon and then we flew right over it.  Oh, what an amazing view!   We flew around the canyon for 15-20 minutes, over to the north rim, right over the Colorado river which looked like a stream below but which was 350 feet wide.  We could see the rapids.   Cory, the pilot, gave us great information and we were all able to ask questions - we could all hear through the headphones what everyone was saying.   He clearly has a love for the Canyon and was a really interesting guide.  He named the various peaks, talked about wildlife, pointed out the nearby 
San Francisco mountain peaks, etc.   We were very happy with the time we were over the Canyon - we'd feared we'd only fly over for 5 mnutes but we saw such alot.   We all agreed it was one of, if not THE, best experiences of our lives.  It cost quite alot but it was absolutely worth it.   If you think the view from the Rim is incredible, just fly over it - you'll be stunned.

review_text:
Truly outstanding airplane ride on one of the loveliest places on earth.  I'm a long-time pilot but somehow never managed to ride in a bi-plane, so it was a dream come true for me to finally get to ride in one  (now if only I could have flown it too! ;)  

There are lots of ways you can see Kauai by air.  None are cheap. But every other method has you watching out a window like it's TV screen.  Take this trip and you directly experience the island with all your senses, you're not just a passive viewer.

Our pilot Kevin has been doing this a long time and clearly loves his job.  With so many movies filmed here and so few pilots over the years available, Kevin has had a lot of fun experiences working with film crews and actors over the years and has plenty of fun stories to tell during the flight, in addition to the standard descriptions of the sights,

If you are wondering how safe the trip is, then as a pilot I can tell you that you are in very good hands with this outfit.  The plane is obviously extremely well cared for (and loved!) and in excellent condition, the pilot is very safety-conscious, and he isn't a show-off that puts you in danger.  This is a solid operator that knows how to do it right, you are in good hands here.   

And if you worry about the open-cockpit aspect: you'll have a cloth helmet and goggles, and you are actually not really in the airstream unless you go out of your way to get into it while peering over the side to something down below.  With the wing above you for shade, no worries about getting too much sun, and the air is not cold.  It's actually a really pleasant experience in the open cockpit that you will really like!

Bottom line: truly unique experience for one or two passengers, from a very safe outfit who knows what they are doing.  There simply isn't a better flying experience on the island.

Head gear with headphones are provided so you can talk back and forth to the pilot (all you need to complete the outfit is a scarf). I've done at least a dozen copter tours on the islands and now this is my 2nd fixed wing tour. I know another reviewer disagrees on some points, but here's my take based on my fixed wing experience today:
Fixed wing over copter:
1.  Price... I paid less than half for a tour that covered much of the same areas as the similar length copter tours. HALF! - 
2.  Comfort - Much roomier than most copters. 
3.  Window - Everyone has a window seat. Not always true on even the 4 seat copters as 2 of you on the small copter may be in the front seat (meaning one of your windows is the front of the windshield.But, sometimes parts of the plane may invade your photos. Least view impairment is with a fixed wing plane with the wing on top.
4. Feeling of being solid - I LOVE copter tours especially as the doors off tours, but there are moments of jerks and vibration that you don't have on the fixed wing plane. 

Copter beats fixed wing tour: 
1.  Copters in Hawaii tend to go up more canyons which allow more ops to see water falls. 
2.  At certain places, the copter may choose to hover and turn to allow you an optimal view or photo op (Jack Harter Tours on Kauai has a tour 30 minutes longer than most that does this a lot)
3.  When all is said and done, I think the view from the 3 outside window seats is slightly better especially when you fly a doors-off copter tour.  

Summary:  I think the fixed wing tour is an excellent way to get the wonders of the islands from the air, yet save enough per couple for 2 or 3 high-end dinners here. If you're a bit timid about air tours, I think the fixed wing is less intimidating. I think the best photo op experiences remains the copters with doors off, but certainly one can get credible photos from the fixed wing.

After take-off the plane headed South and this is only some of the things we saw -- the incredible Kipu Kai shoreline, Poipu, Olokele Canyon (I actually saw the famed Robinson family's house!), many different angles & views of the Waimea Canyon which is a MUST for any Kauai visitor and then an outstanding tour or the 
Nā Pali coast.  Brian, our pilot was flawless with his detail and was really entertaining about all these sites and more.  The view of the "cathedrals" along the Nā Pali coast was very amazing!

We then wrapped around the North Shore at Ke'e Beach which is the end of the road on North Shore & start of the 12-mille ea. way Kalalau Trail along the Nā Pali coast. Extending the North Shore we then had amazing views of Tunnels Beach, Ha'ena, Lumaha'i Beach, Hanalei & all Hanalei Bay...and then Princeville.

Brian then flew us inland up the Hanalei River valley & as close as we could get to Mount Waiʻaleʻale at over 5,000 feet, almost always shrouded in clouds as it was for us, on the summit as this is one of the wettest spots in the world with over 600 inches of rain per year.

Just think GREEN & BLUE because this is what you will see.

GREEN because that is what you see on this airplane tour of the many remote places on the land of Kauai and BLUE for all the beautiful water you see and then including beaches, reefs, Hanalei valley & taro fields, the Wailua River and TONS of waterfalls.

We took this sightseeing flight around the island Kauai with Air Ventures. Their website is www.airventureshawaii.com. We paid $125 per person for a 1 hr tour. The tour was in an air van that seats 6 people plus the pilot. It was comfortable. The pilot talked to us through our headphones and we asked questions using a microphone. We saw the whole island, the coffee plantations, Waimea (Grand) Canyon, the famous waterfalls in Jurassic Park, the Na Pali Coast, the beaches and golf courses, Julia Robert's house and even a whale slapping the water with his fluke. The tour itself was great. But the wait was ridiculous. We were picked up near the cruise ship terminal at 9:15 am and arrived at the airport at 9:20 am. The tour was supposed to start at 10:00 am, but it did not start until nearly 11:00 am. Since our time in port was short, every minute counts so we did not like having to hang around the airport when we could have been sitting at the beach or shopping.

review_text:
The good: smooth ride on a windy day and spectacular views that can only be seen from the air.
Since it has been a rainy week on the island, we got to see tons of rushing waterfalls which was super cool!  
The bad:  The "air conditioned cabin was stuffy with a weak flow of lukewarm air coming from the vents.  The intrusive chatter over the headset was annoying, as was the choice of music.  The flight would be greatly enhanced with some soothing hawaiian instrumental music without the mediocre vocals.  Our pilot/guide, Harry, was an excellent pilot but needs to work on his narrative, which was far from entertaining, barely informative and delivered in a monotone that drove me nuts.  I would have rather he simply flown the plane.
But it is a great value for your dollar on this expensive vacation paradise, especially if you get the Aloha card at your timeshare.  Perhaps my expectations were too high as I had hoped to be regaled with local legend and interesting facts beyond "that is tunnels beach....that is wiamea canyon....those are waterfalls....that is the largest coffee plantation in usa....."  Plus, our 60-70 min tour was more like 55 min.

When you are on a cruise with 4 days at 4 different Hawaiian Islands, you cannot do everything you would like. At Kauai, my wife and I decided that to get a sense of the Island, an airplane or helicopter ride would give you a good snapshot of the varied topography. We opted for the slower (and cheaper) one-hour airflight. We were not disappointed. We could both see well out of separate windows. We started off by following the south coast with its resorts and beaches and circled to see the famous Spouting Horn blowhole. Even though there was some cloud (to be expected in winter months) the Na Pali cliffs with inland waterfalls were awesome and the rain forest fascinating showing trees with different shades of green. The transformation from rain forest to the desert-like Waimea Canyon with its multicolored layered rocks was dramatic as we flew over it and into the sheer valleys. On the way back we had a bonus of seeing the Sleeping Giant, the Wailua River (with barges leading to the Fern Grotto), the Wailua Falls,  and the cruise ship in Nawiliwili Harbor. Our pilot was most knowledgeable mentioning his preferences on the scenery and pointing out locations where films had been made or houses owned by film stars. As a result of our flight, we would like to revisit the Island and spend more time there.

review_text:
I don't know how I got so lucky.  I weighed the right amount.  But I got to sit in the co-pilot seat.  My friend asked the pilot to make sure I didn't try to fly.  It looked like I could have if I had known how.  Great views over the most beautiful island in the world.  The views are just enough distant to provide good perspective.  The view I treasured the most was just before we got to Waimea Canyon.  We could see from the west into three waterfalls that fall 3,000 feet from Mt. Waialiali (sp?) the wettest place on earth.  They seemed to spill from the clouds that shroud the top of the mountain.  I had been on a helicopter tour of the island before but don't remember seeing that view.
The pilot, Harry, was wonderful, charming and informative and so helpful.  The take off and landing were soft,  not in the least scary or jarring.  Unfortunately, one of the rear passengers got sick.  It did not affect me, but the persons closer did not like that part of the trip.  Very good experience for the money.

After taking the Air Ventures tour, now I've seen Kauai from underwater, SCUBA Diving in Poipu, from the Sea on a Catamarran Sunset Dinner Cruise on the Ka Napoli Coast, and from land at the Smith Family Luau, then "Tubing the Ditch" on a closed Sugar Plantation, and a Zip Line trip in Princeville.
The air tour was terrific, we flew over everything I had seen from sea and land. Paul, our pilot narrated the tour, and answered many questions even before they were asked. He pointed out waterfalls that we never could have seen in any other tour, also homes of local movie stars.  Paul is an exceptional pilot, and as I found out, also a flight instructor. review_text:
On our recent trip to Kauai I really wanted to take an aerial tour of the island, but was discouraged by the helicopter companies policy of gouging big people for a ride. I'm 6'6" and just shy of 300 lbs, and the helicopter operators charge you for an extra seat. 
I discovered AirVentures online, and for just a little over a hundred dollars had a GREAT air tour. 
The staff was super friendly....very Aloha!! I got the seat in back right by the door, with no seat in front of it, and was able to stretch my legs fully out on the ride, and was able to easily see out of both sides of the plane. Our pilot was really cool, and talked with us a lot during the trip.
The ride itself was awesome!! The headphones made the noise minimal, and communications were easy. The takeoff was smooth as can be, and the flight very comfortable. There were a few bumpy parts here and there, but really nothing major. We saw all of the sights from Poipu, up Waimea Canyon, all along Napali, the North Shore beaches, Hanalei Valley, and inland to Waileilei, then over the East Shore before landing back in Lihue. 
While we didn't dive into the canyons like the helicopters do (although watching the helicopters below us, I thought they got a bit too close for comfort) we flew low enough to see everything in great detail. And there was no "wasted" time flying over the water as somebody had previously posted. 
AirVentures Kauai is an excellent value....if you dont want to pay the exorbinant charges the helicopter companies charge, book this flight....you WILL NOT be disappointed!!
One last thing, if it is the only splurge you take on your trip....do not miss flying over Kauai. It is honestly the most beautiful sight I have ever seen.

review_text:
On the positive side: Our pilot was very informative and friendly, we got to see a lot that we wouldn't have otherwise seen (partially because our boat trip was cancelled 3 times due to weather, so this was our only chance to see the Napali coast). Negative side: I have never been so motion sick in my life. I really don't mean to whine, I've never had trouble with this before, and neither has my husband, but both of us were absolutely miserable for about 3/4 of the trip. The weather was bad, so I'm sure that didn't help, and we were in the back of the plane (I have no idea if that makes a difference or not). I've been on a helicopter tour before this one, and relatively small planes, and have never had this problem, so I'm not sure what caused it, but the tour was not nearly as enjoyable as it could have been. The other negative (which might have also been because of the weather) was that we didn't get to see Jurassic Falls at all, or any waterfalls close up, and we also didn't get a DVD at the end, so I did feel a little bit cheated despite the great price because of what I knew others had seen on the same tour. 

Overall, I would recommend this company to a friend, it was a memorable experience and, since it was storming every other day of our trip, this was our only good view of the island. I originally wanted to give it fewer stars because I felt so miserable and we didn't get to see several of the things I thought we would, but I realize that most of that is not the company's or pilot's fault. The pilot appeared to have some decent time logged (I did hear the stall horn sound for a couple seconds a couple times, though, which isn't horrible but not optimal) and the plane is an Airvan, which are used for things like search and rescue, civil air patrol, etc. so the plane is a good size and very durable when well-maintained.

If we do another air tour somewhere else, we'll probably spring for one by helicopter; plane rides are less expensive (1/3 to 1/4 less, if I recall correctly) and are generally safer, but they can't get up-close-and-personal like helicopters can.

review_text:
My wife, daughter and I were on our way to Andros Island in the Bahamas and we thought booking a charter through Miami Seaplane to get us there might be a neat experience.   It was fantastic!

Nicolle was amazing as she helped us with our reservation details.  She was very patient with my endless list of questions and she always responded to my inquiries right away.  She helped us with a few luggage issues and worked hard to accommodate all of our needs.

Tony was our pilot.  What a great guy!  He's also a great pilot.  I've been on many float planes before, but I've never seen a pilot land one as smoothly as Tony did on this trip.  His ability to thread the (cloud) needle was also very impressive.  He helped us successfully navigate the Customs/Immigration office in Bimini and he even waited in the Customs office for us so that we could grab a quick bite to eat while the officers arrived.  

The flight was indescribably beautiful.  The Caribbean Sea is gorgeous from the shore in my opinion, but the view from 2000 feet was more than breathtaking.  Tony made sure to point out all the landmarks we passed on the way as well as letting us know when we were about to pass over a ray or shark on the flats.  The flight has forever left my family with many great memories.

Unfortunately when it was time for us to return Tropical Storm Emily showed up and we had to, for safety reasons, make other arrangements to get home.  One would expect the folks at Miami Seaplane Tours to simply say "see ya next time" but that is not what happened.  Nicolle kept me updated on the situation hourly.  It worked best for me to make arrangements for my wife and daughter to fly home via New York so they could avoid the storm.  I needed to get to Miami to collect some of our luggage (We were in North Carolina the week before our trip to Andros and we had more "stuff" packed than we could safely take on the Seaplane) so I flew to Miami via Atlanta just as the storm subsided.  Miami was a bit of a mess after the storm.  In some parts of the city people were actually kayaking instead of driving.  Despite this Tony went and collected our bags from the storage area and delivered them to me personally.  That was over and above the call of duty in my opinion, but the Miami Seaplane Tours folks take their customer service seriously!

My wife and I are small business owners and it's always fun for us to see how other people run their small businesses.  Some (more than a few to be honest) small businesses have lousy service and terrible people working for them.  Miami Seaplane Tours is just the opposite..................their customers receive great service from simply wonderful people.

I can't wait to fly with them again!

review_text:
My 11 year old son and myself rode in the Cessna 172 pictured on this page. We booked a 1 hour "Ultimate Tour" and had picture perfect weather.  Initially, I was a little concerned because the location on Rickenbacker Causeway seemed like a backup or satellite location (Better signage would help), and when no one was there 15 minutes after our appt timed, I called.  No sooner than this, Capt Adrian appeared with the plane.

Once on shore, he immediately apologized and took ownership, stating the cause of the delay (Honesty and responsibility? +10 points!)  We then loaded quickly, had a quick safety review, then the engine started. We started gliding across the water, and quicker than I thought, we were airborne!

We were airborne in no time and headed out over the main beach.  For anyone not used to low level flying, prepare to be amazed and what you can see, and the overall experience!  Amazing detail, and you experience Miami and the earth in a whole new way.  Being overhead also gives a new dimension to the water, which you can now see through to the bottom in most places.

But nowhere is this better than flying over Biscayne National Park, which is entirely underwater.  Our pilot/instructor Adrian narrated the entire flight, explaining sites, significance, history, and even one illegal lobster trap!  

The water here spans the full pallet of blue to green, with an emphasis on unbelievable glowing light blue that my camera sadly couldn't duplicate.  Depths of water here ranged from 10" to 8 feet, and you can easily spot lots of rays and sharks, especially when we dipped low, and slowed a bit.

Yes, this is a bit more expensive, but any type of aviation is not cheap. But the dividends are well worth it, and formed memories for my son that will last a lifetime!

Great Job Miami Seaplanes! We will be back!

This is a brilliant company to do it with, we arrived 30 minutes early but that was no bother for them, and we were soon up in the air.  We also had the plane to ourselves which was a real treat!
Our pilot was very knowledgeable and great at telling us about the scenery below.  The views were simply stunning, check out my pics!  
P.s. this was my first seaplane ride so i was a little apprehensive, to any first timers, there is absolutely nothing to be worried about, we had the smoothest ride ever, I can't wait to do it again.

I treated my wife to a NorCal Seaplane Excursion for her bday, and it did not disappoint. Admittedly, neither of us had every been in a seaplane before; so we didn't exactly have many benchmarks to compare against. Nevertheless, the experience was truly epic, and we'll remember it for a long time. Taking off, we flew around the headlands of Marin, cruising past Mt. Tam en route to a fly by of Golden Gate. I had never seen the bridge from that vantage point before...it's was truly awesome. Thereafter, we spent some time flying over the main sites of sf: Golden Gate Park, The Haight, Dolores Park, Downtown, North Beach / Coit Tower, the Wharf, etc. Having lived in many of those spots, it was cool to check them out from the sky!
This was amazing.  From the greeting we got when we arrived, to the moment we landed, this trip did not disappoint in any sense.

review_text: In a moment of madness I booked the Seaplane adventure.  It was a little expensive, but we were only in San Francisco for 4 nights and I wanted to do something special.  I need not have worried, we were picked up (a little late), driven across the golden gate bridge (a nice 'free' extra!), and taken to the sea plane.  What an experience! The pilot was fantastic, witty and entertaining.   He helped us into the back of the plane, and took a flight around the San Francisco Area, pointing out landmarks and points of interest.  I was sad when the flight was over.  The flight itself was a lot smoother than I was expecting, and I felt safe and secure the whole time.  The flight over the bridge itself was amazing.  Highly recommended.  Also the taxi driver was really nice and chatty

We booked this trip because it also provided us with two tickets to Alcatraz once the Seaplane Tour had ended.  We were picked up in front of the Hard Rock Cafe at 9:00 am. The van was on time. 
We then drove to the Seaplane base in Sausalito, signed the necessary forms and boarded with two other couples. Each person has a window seat. We flew over the Golden Gate Bridge, Alcatraz prison, AT&T stadium, Muir Woods and SanFrancisco city itself. Our pilot, John , has been flying for over 50 years. He was great and all of us felt comfortable with him at the controls.  I only have one suggestion that the company write a two or three sentence description of each place John points out.  Otherwise he really does not have the time to elaborate on each point of interest we were flying over. 
      Each person wears earphones to keep engine noise to a minimum and provide a communication link between the pilot and passengers.  If you ask a question speak loudly into the microphone provided. It’s voice activated and needs a strong voice to activate it . 
     Management worked very hard with the Hotel Zoe Concierge, Aiyaz Ali, to confirm our flight and the two Alcatraz tickets.  Everything worked out fine. The flight lasted a half hour and John flew us over most areas twice so passengers on both sides of the plane had the same quality view and the ability to take photos with their cameras or smart phones. Once the trip was over , the pilot borrowed our cameras and took pictures of each couple standing on one of the pontoons. We were then driven back across the Golden Gate Bridge again and dropped off at the Hard Rock Cafe. We then walked down to the Alcatraz pier and exchanged our vouchers for afternoon tickets to The Alcatraz prison. You will need to show a photo ID to pick up the Alcatraz tickets and show that ID again twice when you board the afternoon ferry.

review_text:
A great trip in so many ways. For a few extra dollars you can get picked up by vehicle at Fishermans Wharf and driven across the Bridge . We had a beautiful clear weather day, difficult to believe the stories about the fog. 
The plane is an old lady of the skies, 1959 ( I think ) but serves the purpose beautifully.
For the first time in my life weighing 16 stone was a bonus - as heaviest passenger I got to sit in the co-pilot seat but everyone had a decent view. Taxi past Salsalito and then up and away. We chose 45 minute flight which on a clear day was definitely right decision. It takes a few minutes to really relax and it gave me time to enjoy taking in the instruments and mechanics of flying this old plane as well as the views - and what views. Pilot was informative and funny and was happy to answer questions  ( goegraphical and aeronautical) . Having been up and down the coast at sea you then fly right over the Bridge and along  the city frontage before turning right over the City and heading back over Alcatraz. Always just a hint of nerves as you land but smooth and safely down. Back on the mooring pontoon a chance to pose for pictures standing on the float of "your" seaplane! The whole thing is a real treat for boys ( and girls) from 6 to 66!
Great tour, great pilot and amazing landing :) a must do while in San Fran... enjoy you wont regret, (unless your landing was not as good as ours :) )

review_text:
Having visited SF 2 years ago and seen everywhere from ground level we wanted to do something that was that little bit more special and something we had never done before.

In one word it was AWESOME. The weather that day was brilliant with unexpected unrestricted views (no haze) and the sea was like a mill pond. Getting in a plane that is parked on water is an experience in itself and once the safety brief was carried out the taxi to the take off point and the take off itself was a wonderful visual and emotional experience. It is difficult to describe what it is like as the aircraft accelerated to take off speed, skimming across the sea as it did so.
 
Once airborne our decision to take the flight was rewarded a thousand times and more. Words can not describe the excitement  of looking down on San Francisco, The Golden Gate, Alcatraz, The Piers and all the other areas and attractions we flew over. Our pilot made this a very personal experience despite the number of flights he had already made and he provided us with a good description and information on all the parts of our flight.
As with all experiences the 45 minutes were soon gone and it was back to base and a landing experience that was all as good if not better than the take off.
I had done a few hundred flights when I did skydiving as a hobby so I was used to being in a small plane but that did not dull the experience of taking off and landing on water it really is one for the bucket list. If you haven't done it yet trust me you MUST.

My wife on the other hand has little or no experience of small planes and was a little nervous prior to the flight BUT she loved every minute and would have gone back to do it again. She said she always felt safe and trusted both the aircraft and pilot!

Thanks to everyone at Seaplane Adventures, this was a special birthday experience for me and you made it a stunning one.

I booked a Seaplane trip in October 2013 for a flight in April 2014. The day of flight flight arrived (my last day in San Francisco) and I spent the morning heading to Pier 39 for pick up.

When I called the office I was advised no flights were operating that day and although apologetic the staff couldn't understand how the online reservation system let me book for a day when no flights were operating. I "slipped" through the system. I was promised a refund would happen immediately. 

After 12 days I still hadn't received my refund and I emailed 3 times with no response. I finally called (8 hours time difference) and was advised that my refund had "failed". No effort had been made to check or resolve this in those 12 days. I do now finally have my refund. 

I'd recommend being 100% sure your flight is going to happen before wasting precious holiday time getting to an agreed pick up point (at cost) only to be let down. Thoroughly disappointed.

review_text: We took the tour when staying in Moab because we were interested in seeing Canyonlands, which is not easily accessible by car (and certainly not easily traversable). We took the extended tour, which included Arches and although we had explored this at ground level in some detail it was nevertheless interesting to experience the aerial views as well. The pilot was knowledgeable and added interesting stories and was very good at pointing things out. A couple of points though: the planes are small (ours was a five seater) so expect a bumpy ride - there are sick bags to hand; there is very limited leg room - if you are tall it could be uncomfortable; and the headphones are a bit crackly and need adjustment - so best to do this before the commentary starts. In terms of taking pictures, some seats are better than others because of obstruction by the wings. MY wife was OK, despite the turbulence but I was feeling a little queasy - but would not have missed the experience. I would have put this down as a must do when in Moab. The airport is around 16 miles north of Moab so one needs to allow time to get there - some of the flights start fairly early e.g. 08:30. We had a slight wait for a passenger who failed to turn up - just as well as we are not sure where he would have sat! As space is very limited it is best to leave all that you can in the car - camera and water only for the plane!

It might not be the best option for people afraid of heights, although my wife falls into that category, and while she was nervous she still made it down. Everything about this was well put together.  They had someone pick us up at our resort and bring us to their hangar.  They had free water, coffee and snacks available.  We boarded a small Cessna plane and took about an hour and fifteen minute flight to the Grand Canyon.  The view is breathtaking as some of the flight is over the GC.  Our pilot got off the plane with us and guided us the rest of the day.  He took us to the helicopter place and we jumped on a chopper that took us down to the bottom of the canyon. I cannot describe how magnificent the Grand Canyon is and you can't beat viewing it from a helicopter.

Once we were at the base of the Canyon, we boarded a pontoon boat and made about a half mile ride down the Colorado River and then floated back to where we started.  We then took the helicopter back "up top" and hopped on a bus that took us to the SkyWalk.  Our original pilot from the plane was always there to point us to our next stop or tell us to meet back somewhere at a particular time.

The SkyWalk was awesome and a little freaky.  It's an engineering marvel and yeah it's a little scary.  There were a couple of drama queens out there just freaking out.  One little thing to note about the SkyWalk, they don't let you take your phone or camera out there so you have to buy their pictures.  They have camera guys out there that will take your picture, and you can chose what pics you want to buy for a horrendous price (you are not obligated to buy anything).  The problem was they were short staffed on camera guys and the ones that were there had some attitude problems.  I didn't buy any pictures out of spite.  You can get just as good of pictures from the area right next to the SkyWalk.

Next they took us to Guano Cafe to eat lunch.  Our guide said it best that it was more like a metal building that served food than a cafe.  The food was not good, seemed like a freezer meal that was only half way warmed up.  I think they would've been better off telling you to just pack your own lunch or eat at some of the concession stands at the SkyWalk.  However, there were a bunch of tables outside and you got to eat lunch overlooking the Grand Canyon which was pretty cool.

Guano Cafe was located at Guano Point.  There's a lot of room to walk around and see the Canyon from a bunch of different places here.  You can climb to the top of Guano Point and see a great 360 view.  If you didn't already know, Guano is bat feces.  This place is called that because there used to be a mining operation from this location that would mine bat droppings out of caves across the canyon.  Apparently, it is a rich fertilizer and used in a lot of consumer products like makeup, etc.  Anyway, you can see the old abandoned mining equipment and just marvel at the Canyon some more.

We headed back to plane and had a narrated flight back (about 1.5 hours).  Although, I don't believe it to be the fault of the pilot, I would be remiss not to mention that the flight back was really, really turbulent (the flight there was not).  My wife got sick and there were no vomit bags.  Luckily, we had some coffee cups still in there from the morning that she used.  I recommend taking some motion sickness meds before the flight back if you are affected by this type of thing as based on other reviews, this is common for the flight back.

In summary, this was a great trip and I would highly recommend it.  Everything from the Skywalk tickets to meal vouchers were included in the total price ($1,300 for two).  We will be going back and taking my parents at some point because this is really bucket list material.

Even though I graduated from Arizona State University and lived in Phoenix for several years, I had never visited the Grand Canyon.  Shocking oversight, I know.  So on my vacation to Phoenix, I decided to correct this by making a day trip with Westwind Air Service.  They are based at Deer Valley Airport in north Phoenix, and their aircraft only seat a few folks, so you won't be part of a huge crowd.  

If you are not a morning person, you may struggle to make departure time: they ask that you be at the airport by 7:30 AM for check-in for your flight.  But trust me, its worth it.  After a briefing about the journey you're about to take, you are escorted to the plane, and departure happens immediately.  An audio program provides you with interesting facts about the history of areas you are flying over, as you proceed over the desert through scenic vistas, rolling valleys and plateaus, and past nearby mountains.  My trip also included a stop at the Sedona airport to pick up a few more passengers, and Sedona has a fascinating air field atop a mesa.

Within ten minutes of landing in Sedona, we were airborne once again, this time heading for the Grand Canyon itself.  The Grand Canyon Signature Tour, which was what I took, will actually take you over the south rim, and you will be treated to some truly spectacular views of one of the seven natural wonders of the world. Turn after turn, the awesome spectacle impresses you with its astonishing scale.  If you can look at it, and not be stunned, that says far more about you than it says about the Grand Canyon or Westwind Air.  There is no better way to take in the Grand Canyon than by air, and Westwind has perfected that experience.

But the tour doesn't there.  Upon landing at the Grand Canyon airfield, you are met by Westwind's partners on this trip, Pink Jeep Tours.  What follows is great half day expedition into the Grand Canyon park, a box lunch, a short hike through park itself with more spectacular vistas, and concludes with an IMAX theater experience about the history of the park itself.  Then its back to the airport for your return journey to Phoenix.

Yes, the tour is not cheap.  But if your staying in Phoenix and want to make a side trip to the Grand Canyon, bear in mind that driving up there will take the better part of four hours.  Westwind can give you a full day of stunning vistas, and you'll back in Phoenix in time for dinner.  So I consider it great value, and can't recommend it highly enough.

I was debating a lower tour or skipping the landing, but if we only come once we should do the best, and it did not disappoint.  

The day we were scheduled to fly, it was forecasted to be rainy all day and I called to rebook for the next day, I highly recommend flexibility in your schedule in case you run into the same thing.  Th e morning of our flight, it was foggy and rainy and we were concerned again, but while spending time in Talkeetna the sun began to peek out and  we were hopeful.

The plane had seats for 10 and we put on oxygen masks over 12000 feet.  Our pilot (Dave/Dan?  sorry!) was awesome!  He pointed out landmarks, told history of the area.  Flight was smooth, he turned the plane so both sides could always see the views.  Denali was beautiful.  He smoothly landed on fresh snow on the glacier, and offered to take several pictures of our family (and did an excellent job of that too).

If you go to Denali, spend the money and do this trip, it will be a favorite family memory for a lifetime!

The views were amazing. They are ever cooperative. We had to reschedule twice due to bad weather but they accommodative. Unfortunately, we were not able to get the tour we booked due to weather (we booked Grand Denali and ended up doing south side) but, they refunded the difference. 
Staff is very friendly, views are amazing and breathtaking. I seriously recommend to do it. 
Only reason i have 1 star less is because the headsets for my wife was not working during the flight. And she was not able to listen to any narration/music. 
Tip: book early in the day so even if the weather is bad, you can reschedule.

This was my first time in a small plane.  The pilot was great and I wasn't nervous at all.  We were lucky enough to have a clear day.  We flew very close to the mountains and glaciers.  The views were stunning.  My photos didn't do them justice.

review_text: I’m always a bit hesitant to schedule flightseeing tours (due to an experience many, many years ago) but decided to give it a try again on this trip. I’m so very glad I did!!  The views were amazing!! Our pilot was great and I’d fly with him again anytime.  He was very conscientious of our wellbeing throughout flight. He pointed out specific areas of interest and details about the glaciers and mountains.  Unfortunately, we weren’t able to complete the glacier landing as originally planned. I appreciate the agency’s communication regarding the safety concerns which were communicated with us prior to the flight. It was was a great experience from check-in to chevk-out. Would love to fly with them again if I’m able to return to Alaska.  Thanks Talkeetna Air for a great experience!!

My brother-in-law and I were originally booked on the early morning Grand Denali tour with glacier landing. That tour was cancelled due to the weather, so we were rebooked for later that day.  The weather also caused that tour to be cancelled, but we were offered the Southside tour with glacier landing while being cautioned that the chance of landing was low.  Although we were disappointed, we accepted the offer. Were we ever happy we did!  Although clouds prevented us from seeing Denali, the views we did see were amazing.  Before boarding, our pilot (Asa) asked if anyone wanted to sit in the co-pilot’s seat, and I got lucky - so my view was especially incredible. We travelled up Ruth Glacier, and down Tokositna Glacier, and Asa turned the airplane so that everyone could see the sights regardless of the side they were sitting on.  We were unable to make a glacier landing, but in the end it didn’t matter - both of us were very happy with the tour we received.  Also, we received a refund for the difference between the cost of the original tour and the tour we took immediately. Highly recommended!

What ab incredible experience!  This was the highlight of my trip to Alaska.  Words cannot describe how beautiful it is up there.  It is difficult to see Mt Denali from the ground. Before this I saw the mountain peaking through the cloud cover. However when you get up in a plane,the views are breathtaking.  Definitely include the glacier landing.

Despite the moderate weather, it was a very successful sightseeing flight with a glacier landing (actually a MUST).
It is very impressive to immerse yourself in this sometimes bizarre world of rock, snow and glaciers.

My girlfriend is a nervous flier, and our pilot made her feel extremely safe. She explained that she is a mother and she had been flying since she was a kid. review_text: We had a clear day. Rare, I'm told. The experience was amazing. To float above, among, between and land on the Denali mountain range with a photo to be had every 20 seconds makes you go 'should I not just be looking and soakin' it all in?' or 'shouldn't I be taking every photo I can?'For those who choose looking and soaking, then bring your polaroid glasses, it gets bright up there with all that snow, not to mention clouds. If you are landing on the glacier then sunburn cream is a good idea to wear, and take gloves and hat to keep your ears warm (it'll be 5-10 degrees colder than at the airport).For those who choose taking every photo you can, then a polaroid filter will bring out the best shots. Also if you can sit up the front this is definitely the time to use your panorama photo feature on your phone as you'll get front and side views that can only be captured this way, unless you have really wide angle lense. The advantage of not sitting up the front is that your windows are not curved and your camera can focus a whole lot easier on your subject. If there are two of you going on this trip make sure you sit on either side of the aisle so you can get different shots, you can share them later.Generally the air is smooth, its not the tropics with air rising and getting turbulent, this is cold air not doing much. But if you are airsick prone, looking through a camera eyepiece looking at land in motion, with the airplane turning will only make you more airsick sensitive. My advice (being a pilot)   in that regard is to a) take your motion sickness tablet at least half hour before take off b) have something in your stomach already ie breakfast or lunch b) take a piece of candy you can suck on the first time you get a hint of sickness c) take pictures angled forward rather than directly out the side (sense of motion is less) d) don't take pictures when the plane banks. e) look at the horizon after every photo to get your sense of up or down reset in your mind.Last suggestion, for those who put their pictures into photo books, you might want to take a few pictures of the video being played in the snow shoe fitting area. The shots I took were of the aircraft flying and landing on the glacier. These are going to be difficult to get in real life and will be handy for your photo story. This trip on a clear day is a must do for those who appreciate Gods handiwork, for those who love geography, for those who love flying and mostly for those who love photography.

review_text:
Our flight-seeing experience started in downtown Talkeetna at the cozy information/reservation office. There the representative used a cool 3D map of the mountain range to show us exactly where each of the tour options went and what was included in each. He was exceptionally helpful in describing all aspects of the tours, comparing and contrasting them and offering insights regarding the day’s weather and its possible impact on the flights. We ultimately chose the Grand Denali Tour and received directions to the Air Taxi airfield.

When we arrived to check in, we filled out the paperwork, were weighed in (the planes have a weight limit), and were directed to the storage area for the glacier boots. We told the desk person that we did not reserve a glacier landing tour. She whisked us outside and explained in hushed tones that we were being upgraded – no extra charge. They had a glacier flight that was not full; we would complete the seating (if we didn’t mind). We didn’t! 

So far, so good. We got our boots and relaxed on the large deck overlooking the airstrip. We waited and watched a constant parade of planes take off and land. And we waited. And we waited. For more than an hour we waited our turn while clouds gathered around the mountains in the distance. By the time we boarded our plane, the gorgeous day with wide-open blue skies had turned gray and the “seeing” part of our flight-seeing tour was in jeopardy.  

Sure enough, by the time our plane arrived near Denali, the pilot told us the visibility was too bad for us to make a close approach and fly-around of the mountain. I could not help but think, “There’s a thousand bucks down the toilet.” 

Nonetheless, we veered off and made our way to Mt. Foraker, the second largest of the mountains, as well as Mt. Hunter, the third largest. We flew close in to both and along the way traversed mountain valleys, zoomed over other peaks and followed glacial paths, viewing the brilliant colors, the deep crevasses and the sparkling open waters that dotted the tops. Each bank around a mountain’s edge brought more awe-inspiring scenery. As we dove down into another pass, our pilot announced our descent toward the glacier. As one side of the mountain pass opened below us, we could see a makeshift airfield at the far end of a second valley. We turned toward the site and were soon skimming over the snow and ice, taxiing in next to several other tourist planes.

I’m from Michigan. I’ve seen my share of snow. I’ve wandered wilderness areas in the winter. This, however, was other-worldly (think Hoth from Star Wars). We were surrounded by towering cliffs on three sides, with added rivers of snow flowing down between edges, adding to the mass we were on. We walked about the glacier for about a half hour, taking photos, watching other planes take off and land and learning glacier facts from our pilot. Before leaving, our pilot took photos of everyone and gave us the itinerary for the remainder of our flight.     

Taking off from the glacier was an experience. First, we were heading downhill, as the glacier was flowing downward into the large valley we turned from originally. The glacier’s edge dropped off precipitously into the valley, so we had only a limited amount of “runway” – kind of like flying off an aircraft carrier. Lastly, the air currents were dramatically different inside the valley, and they would hit the plane perpendicularly as we flew off the edge of our glacier and into the larger chasm. Fun.  

Believe it or not, it was! How often do you get to experience something like that? Our pilot lifted off and arced into the valley and quickly ascended above the valley walls. Before we knew it, the entire range was again below us and the green flatlands surrounding Talkeetna beckoned us back to the airfield. As an extra on the way back, we saw a large brown bear walking along the shoreline of one of the many lakes below. 

Once back on the ground, our pilot told us that we would be compensated for the disappointment of not viewing Denali – we’d all be getting a partial refund. In our case, this was pretty sweet, as we’d already received a free upgrade. The refund was substantial, too, so it made the overall experience all the better, knowing that the company treated their customers that fairly.

Even without seeing the star of the show, the Talkeetna Air Taxi flight-seeing experience was one I’ll never forget. They have to get a demotion for the long delay between check-in and take-off, which ultimately caused us to miss the view of the summit; however, everything else was absolutely first class. The sales staff and airfield personnel were friendly and professional. Our pilot was excellent and a fine tour guide, too, and Mother Nature set an incredible table for us to enjoy. I felt completely safe and comfortable in the plane, and the headphones worked very well to both reduce engine noise and provide the pilot’s commentary. 

As alluded to earlier, this is not an inexpensive experience. Unless you have a sizeable disposable income, this will likely be a once-in-a-lifetime kind of thing, but it is certainly one to consider, and I think well worth the price – especially if you have a camera with a ton of memory. Anecdotally, I’ve heard that Talkeetna Air Taxi is considered the better of the flight-seeing tours available, and I found nothing that might argue the point. If you get the chance, open the wallet and fly off into the wild blue yonder. You will not regret it (unless you forget that camera).

Our flight was in the afternoon and the office building at the airport was very busy with travelers awaiting flights as well as those who had just returned. All the staff we met were knowledgeable, friendly, and eager to make our experience memorable.  Our pilot, Dave, was highly experienced, confident, thorough, and really fun. Plus he provided a lot of good information on glaciers and the geography of Alaska.  We flew in a turboprop, De Havilland Otter that seated eight-or-so passengers plus the pilot.  The glacier landing was so exciting as the pilot didn't have to descend to land...he just flew until the skis of the aircraft landed on the snowy upward slope which served to slow the aircraft down to taxi speed very quickly...and, it was so quiet as we landed - a truly unique experience. 
 After about 15 or 20 minutes in the snow outside the aircraft, taking photos and watching two other aircraft land on the glacier, we re-boarded  and the pilot pointed the nose down the snowy slop and we glided downhill until we were once again airborne. Flying with Talkeetna Air Taxi was, without a doubt, one of the highlights of our visit to Alaska.  This company and its people have earned our highest recommendation. review_text:
I booked the Mountain Voyager with Glacier Landing flight with Talkeetna Air Taxi. While traveling from Wasilla to Talkeetna, I spotted Denali in the distance -- this was an exciting start to the day. After checking in at the office, I put some booties on over my shoes and boarded the aircraft.  The craft seated ten passengers, and we all had windows. Headsets helped to muffle the engine noise and hear from our pilot (the microphones were not activated). The weather was clear as we headed into the Alaska range, but we encountered some clouds/mist as we first entered the mountains. It was hard to see, and I had to remind myself that these pilots fly these routes every day and weren't going to fly the plane into the side of a mountain! Thankfully, the clouds cleared soon. The views of the snow, ice, and glaciers below were stunning. Now and then, we'd get a glimpse of bright blue ice below. Then we spotted the peaks of Denali -- the the highest mountain peak in North America. One of the main reasons I took this flight was to increase my chances of seeing it, and fate was on my side this day. It was breathtaking to see the crisp white snow against a brilliant blue sky, with its own little cloud on top.  I had lots of time to snap some photos and video as we slowly moved from north to east peaks.
We landed on Ruth Glacier, where we all stepped out on to the snowy surface (thank goodness for the booties)! We had ample time to walk around a bit and take photos. There were maybe a half dozen other planes around, and it was interesting to watch them take off and land.  I had a moment that literally took my breath away when I took a step and my foot sunk down about 18" beneath the snow!  But I laughed as I was startled, and was not hurt in any way. We were also able to get a few more glimpses of Denali as the clouds just beneath the mountain top shifted in the light breeze.
I could not have asked for a better experience -- well worth the price and a memory that will be a highlight of my first time in Alaska!!

The biggest piece of advice I can offer is to try to be flexible with trying to do a flight seeing tour of Denali.  The weather around the mountains is just about impossible to predict and heavy cloud cover around the mountains is common.

This is our second tour with TAT.  We flew with them about 16 years ago when it was just my wife and I.  This time it was a three generation group of six of us.  We had planned to to the "Grand Denali" tour and had it booked for our first full day in Talkeetna.  However, the clouds were not cooperating that day and they had actually not gone up for any flights.  Over the course of the next couple of days, we rescheduled a few times and juggled some of the other activities that we had planned.  Finally, on our last morning before heading to Anchorage to fly home, the weather cleared enough to allow a flying tour of the glaciers and lower peaks.  Denali itself was initially not visible, but we dressed for the potential for the glacier.

The tour itself was excellent.  Our pilot/guide was very familiar with the area, the landmarks on the ground, and the geological characteristics of the area we toured.  His communication to us was excellent, and I was even more impressed with his communication with the other flights operating.  Ours was the first flight of the morning, so he was also acting as a scout to pass back to others how conditions were looking.

He made several looks at potential glacier landing spots, but all were too cloudy to bother with.  Finally, near the end of our time, the glacier area that serves as base camp for those who set out to climb Denali was clear.  We were able to make the glacier landing.  Mt. Foraker had the best visibility and we took most of our group pictures in front of it.  However, the peak of Denali was also visible for a while during our stop and we got to appreciate just how big of a rock it is from about 15 miles from the peak.  Our pilot took lots of great pictures with our phones and my camera of our group and helped make an incredible memory that we will all carry forever.

I highly recommend flying with these folks.

review_text:
I had always thought these trips were too expensive, and probably not worth it - thus passing on several opportunities.  This trip we went ahead and booked one, and then tried over several days to actually make the trip, as the weather was preventing flying - pushing the trip back further and further.  We almost cancelled rather than drive two hours (one way) to make a final attempt, but things looked good - so we went for it, and got in the air.

Once in a lifetime is an over-used phrase.  In this case, it is absolutely spot on!  I won't spoil it by giving you details of things that can't adequately be described with words, and instead will give advice...

Weather can be particularly uncooperative for these trips, so it's best to schedule your overall trip to allow many attempts at getting in the air.  The staff is amazingly capable and willing to work with you to get you into the air when you can, but you want to give them lots of chances if your scheduled attempt fails.

Make sure your camera and phone batteries are charged.

Layer your clothing so that you can be wrapped up like the kid in A Christmas Story, or shirtless like the crazy kid on our trip.  You can never be sure what will be best.

Wear waterproof shoes, but they don't need to be perfect.  They have shoe covers if you need them.  Bring good sunglasses.

Pee before you get on the plane

Be prepared to spend time in Talkeetna waiting for your flight if the weather is bad.  There's lots to see and do.

But passengers can only see out the side of the plane.  So in essence, the only view you get of the peak is when he flies alongside the mountain. review_text:
This was really difficult to rate.  The experience itself (flying around Denali and landing on a glacier) is a full 5 star experience.  If there was no other operator in Talkeetna, I would have rated this company higher, just based on how cool the experience is.  (If you are wondering whether or not to splurge on a flight around Denali - do it, it's AMAZING).  But this is a review of Talkeetna Air Taxi - the tour operator, not just a review of the scenic flight, and honestly, I wasn't that impressed with TAT.

After reading all the positive reviews, I chose to book with Talkeetna Air Taxi.  I completed the online booking form and entered my credit card info.  When I received my confirmation a few days later, I noted I had been scheduled for a different day than requested.  Not the end of the world - I contacted the company, they apologized and rescheduled me for the correct day - but if I hadn't read my confirmation carefully, I'm sure it would been a much bigger deal to fix the day I was supposed to fly.  Then about a week later, I received a voicemail letting me know they had needed to change the time of my flight - but the time they told me it was changed to was the time they had told me in the first place.  Again, no big deal, but it did make me wonder how organized they were.

When my family arrived at the office on the day of our flight it was quite chaotic.  People were landing and trying to buy t-shirts, people were checking in and needing to fill out forms and get weighed.  When my turn to check in arrived, I asked how the weather was expected to be.  I received a curt - "your flight will be fine" in response.  I was asking, because we had planned to be in Talkeetna for a couple of days and had booked our flight right at the start so that we could postpone/reschedule if weather dictated.  I got the feeling they were just too busy to talk to me.

Our flight was delayed by about 10 minutes, again - not a big deal, but we were waiting outside in the cold rain for those 10 minutes and no one from the company provided us with any information.

There was heavy cloud cover when we took off.  During the first portion of our flight, the clouds completely enveloped the plane - nothing but white-out conditions outside my window.  I have to tell you - I was nervous!  Denali and the mountains around it stuck up out of the cloud cover and so the main portion of our flight was still amazing.  The return was also completely clouded in.  I do wish I had the opportunity to talk about the weather before the flight.  Maybe they would have convinced me this was still the best chance, given how changeable the weather is, but since I never got to discuss it with them, I just don't know.

My other big complaint was that the pilot provided almost no commentary during the flight.  He seemed a competent pilot, but he wasn't at all personable.  There were many points during the flight where I really didn't know what I was looking at.  I would have preferred an audio recording to the silence we mostly got.  It also would have been nice for him to give a reassuring "don't worry about the clouds around Talkeetna, you'll see Denali just fine," during the first portion of the flight.  I am particularly contrasting this experience to the wonder commentary provided by the pilot during my Misty Fjords scenic flight.

I know this review sounds fairly negative.  I wasn't really that bad, I'm just balancing it against how much the trip cost and how many other operators there are that offer the same service.  If you are anywhere near Talkeetna, you should definitely do a scenic flight around Denali and spend the extra to land on a glacier - it truly is an amazing experience.  My experience with Talkeetna Air Taxi was perfectly adequate, but that's all.

The trip was a highlight of our vacation, and would highly recommend them to anyone looking for a flight seeing tour.  You will NOT regret it.

This was a phenomenal experience. Of course the scenery was breathtaking. This activity is WELL worth the money. It is an expensive outing, but such a wonderful experience.

There are several companies in the area offering similar service, but TAT was fantastic. We were scheduled for one day but had bad weather. They were very flexible to reschedule us for another day (and so friendly about it). When we arrive for our flight, they still were not sure if we could land on the glacier so they did not take our payment before we left. All the front desk staff was friendly and helpful. The pilot did a great job of flying and narrating the trip. Don't be scared of the small planes - the ride was very smooth. Turbulence isn't a huge problem in Alaska because there isn't enough heat to make the air unstable. My husband and I took motion sickness meds just in case. The glacier landing was well worth the additional money. It was such a unique experience.

Bottom line - spend the money for this experience and go with TAT! They are great!

Probably one of the most spectacular things I have ever seen, our flightseeing tour of Denali (Mt Mckinley) in Alaska on Talkeetna Air Taxi was an unforgettable experience. We got the best deal of any of the many local flyers, our pilot Paul was great and everyone was so friendly. We felt safe and reasonably warm for our December flight around the summit. I researched all of the Air Taxis from Anchorage to Talkeetna and chose Talkeetna Air after talking with the locals and they did not disappoint. I highly recommend them to anyone looking for an unforgettable experience.

We had booked our reservation months in advance for a Mt. McKinley (Denali) flightseeing tour with glacier landing.  Unfortunately, the day before our tour we realized that the weather predictions for the following day were not going to be condusive to seeing "the high one".  TAT was awesome and reschuled us for that day at 4:00 pm.

I must say that this was one of the most amazing experiences of my life!  The weather was perfect. We landed on the Ruth Glacier and had some awesome views of Denali.

Alaska was everything we hoped and we will be back!  

PS-TAT has some really cool T-shirts and hats too!

review_text:
Both K2 and Talkeetna Air Taxi (TAT) get my highest recommendation. Follow along with the bouncing ball, kids, as our tale unfolds:

Pre-booked directly with TAT about a month before leaving for Alaska. Our tour train arrived in Talkeetna about noon and we were scheduled to fly with them at 3pm. Walked over to their shop in town at about 1pm and spoke with Chris, who explained  that the weather on the mountain was less than optimum for flightseeing so far that day, and showed us a current computer graphic of the weather system to illustrate the point. We explained that we had only that afternoon available since we were scheduled to leave Talkeetna 11am the following morning. Chris suggested that we kill a few hours in town, cross our fingers, and pray that the weather gods cleared things up enough by early evening to give it a shot. Touched base with him on the hour until 6pm, but the mountain remained fogged in. Sensing our desperation to go up anyway, Chris explained that he'd be happy to fly us around the lower part of the Ruth Glacier on a less extensive tour, but strongly urged us to call it a day since we were likely to be unhappy with the view. Look. When a pilot tells you to cancel...you cancel. We told Chris we'd try him again early the next morning if the weather cleared, and TAT refunded our deposit no questions asked. I have to commend Chris and TAT for their helpfulness and honesty.  

Fast forward to the following morning. We take a look out the back deck of the Talkeetna Alaskan Lodge at 7:45am. The sky is clear and the mountains are in plain view. I call TAT back, but their entire morning schedule is committed to taking up climbers that they were unable to get up the day before, and they can't possibly get us up and back before we have to leave. TAT made their bones depositing climbers on Denali, and understandably they're priority #1. We're out of luck and about out of time.

It's a horrible sight to see a grown man cry. It really is. In a last dicth effort at salvaging the most anticipated part of our trip, I run over to the concierge desk at the lodge and BEG the woman to put us on something...anything...a hot air baloon if necessary... some Wright Brothers pedal-powered contraption...that can get us up to Denali and back by 11am. 

Angels exist. Trust me. I found one. Within 10 minutes, the concierge (who is now a viable candidate for sainthood if she performs just TWO more miracles) called us and set to get ready...she got seats for 4 of us with K2 Aviation at 8:30, and we'd be back in time to make our bus. Take note, my countrymen. I  do solemnly swear that I shall willingly fall upon my sword for this woman should the need ever arise.

Mike at K2 took us up in a 5-seat Cessna for the ride of our lives on their Denali Grand Tour. Nothing compares with the sight of seeing the biggest rock on the North American continent up close and personal. Loss for words. Fill in your favorite superlatives. There's a dreamlike quality to the entire landscape, as if it were some massive painted backdrop for a Cecil B. DeMille film. Mike gave us the 4-1-1 on the geologic environs as we flew around Denali, Foraker, Hunter, the Ruth Glacier and the Talkeetna Mountain range. Absolutely the highlight of our trip to Alaska. It'll be yours, too. 

The flyguys of Talkeetna are a cooperative and close-knit band of brothers who are constantly in radio contact with each other about flying conditions in the area.  You won't find a friendlier, more informative bunch of "Right Stuff"-ers anywhere this side of NASA. Hats off, and sincere thanks to the crews at both K2 AND TAT. 

And, of course, to my guardan angel at the Talkeetna Alaskan concierge desk. Who loves ya, baby?

Strongly suggest that you make arrangements well before you leave for Alaska if you're planning on going on a Denali flight. Space fills up quick (and we got damn lucky). And be prepared on any given day for the mountain to do what the mountain is wont to do. Anything big enough to create its own weather system ain't arranging its day around YOUR schedule. Denali is like a box of chocolates, Forrest...

.

Our top priority in Talkeetna was flightseeing over Mt. McKinley (Denali). We booked with Talkeetna Air Taxi for the Grand Denali tour with Glacier Landing. We had 2 Toursaver books so my family of 4 saved $440. It was cloudy (as usual) so we were thinking that our trip might be a bummer, but boy were we wrong! We had the time of our lives! My hat's off to those pilots, they really know their stuff! The pilot did a great job of stay below the clouds so that we could see the sharp cliffs and massive glaciers. Many times we were so close that the proximity warning would enunciate "500" warning us that we were within 500 feet of the terrain. But I never felt scared. My 12-year old daughter was petrified to board the plane, but soon she began to enjoy herself and now she'll tell you that flightseeing was one of her favorite activities in Alaska. Our glacier landing was as smooth as silk. What an awesome feeling to stand in such a majestic place! After we took-off again, the pilot found a hole in the clouds and after a steep assent we popped out above the clouds for a perfectly clear view of Denali's summit. WOW! If you have any chance to take this trip - DO IT!
